definition_zh: 放弃；抛弃；遗弃；放任；纵情
definition_en: to leave someone or something behind for good, or to give up an aim
core_image: 一个人把钥匙放在桌上，转身离开不再回来
scene: 雨夜里，他把车停在路边，锁上门，沿着公路走远。He decided to abandon the car and walk to the next town.
sceneCN: 这里的 abandon 指「抛弃；丢下」（第 1 个义项：把某物丢下不再管）；句意是他决定丢下车子，步行去下一个镇。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ment 构成，义为「放弃；遗弃」
义为「被遗弃的；放纵的」
义为「遗弃者」

senses.title: To give up an aim
senses.definition: stops trying to do or achieve something
senses.definitionCN: 停止尝试做某事或达成某个目标
senses.example: They had to abandon the climb before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 他们不得不在天黑前放弃登顶。
senses.why: The oldest French sense is to hand something over, and giving up a plan is handing it away.
senses.whyCN: 古法语最古老的意思是「交出去」，放弃计划就是把计划交出去。

senses.title: To leave someone behind
senses.definition: leaves a person without help or support
senses.definitionCN: 丢下某人，不再给予帮助或支持
senses.example: He would never abandon a friend in trouble.
senses.exampleCN: 他绝不会抛弃陷入困境的朋友。
senses.why: To surrender control of a person is to stop standing by them.
senses.whyCN: 把一个人交出去不管，就是不再站在他身边。

senses.title: To desert a place
senses.definition: leaves a building, town or vehicle and does not return
senses.definitionCN: 离开房屋、城镇或车辆且不再回来
senses.example: The villagers abandon their homes when the river rises.
senses.exampleCN: 河水上涨时，村民会弃家而走。
senses.why: A place handed over to itself stands empty, so the verb covers deserted houses and towns.
senses.whyCN: 被交还给自己的地方就空了下来，动词因此涵盖弃屋与弃城。

senses.title: To give up a claim
senses.definition: formally gives up a right, claim or plan
senses.definitionCN: 正式放弃某项权利、主张或计划
senses.example: The company agreed to abandon the lawsuit.
senses.exampleCN: 公司同意放弃这场诉讼。
senses.why: Legal surrender is the literal old sense, still visible in claims and lawsuits.
senses.whyCN: 法律上的让与正是古老的直义，在权利主张与诉讼里仍看得见。

senses.title: To let oneself go
senses.definition: in abandon oneself to, gives way completely to a feeling
senses.definitionCN: 在 abandon oneself to 中完全沉入某种情感
senses.example: She abandoned herself to grief for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 她放任自己悲伤了一个星期。
senses.why: Giving up control of oneself produces the reflexive pattern and the noun abandon.
senses.whyCN: 放弃对自己的控制，便生出反身句型和名词 abandon。

senses.title: To leave a ship
senses.definition: leaves a ship that is in danger
senses.definitionCN: 离开处于危险中的船只
senses.example: The crew had to abandon the sinking ship.
senses.exampleCN: 船员不得不弃掉正在下沉的船。
senses.why: The call abandon ship is the oldest practical use, when a vessel can no longer be saved.
senses.whyCN: 弃船令是最古老的实用场景：船已无法挽救。

senses.title: Complete lack of restraint
senses.definition: in the phrase with abandon, acts freely and without shyness
senses.definitionCN: 在 with abandon 中自由自在、毫不拘束地行动
senses.example: The children danced with abandon in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在雨中尽情跳舞。
senses.why: A person who has surrendered caution moves without holding back, and the noun names that freedom.
senses.whyCN: 放下了谨慎的人不再收着，名词便指这种自由。

senses.title: To stop maintaining something
senses.definition: stops looking after or continuing something
senses.definitionCN: 停止照管或继续某事
senses.example: The council will abandon the old road next year.
senses.exampleCN: 议会明年将不再维护这条旧路。
senses.why: Upkeep is a kind of hold on a thing, and letting go of it is another branch of the same idea.
senses.whyCN: 维护也是对事物的把持，放手不管便是同一观念的另一分支。

intro.en: The word came into English from French, where it meant to put something under someone else's control.
intro.cn: 这个词经法语进入英语，原意是「把某物交到别人掌控之下」。

items.en: a bandon meant at one's disposal or under one's control.
items.cn: a bandon 意为「听凭处置、在他人掌控之下」。

items.en: abandoner meant to give something over to another's power.
items.cn: abandoner 意为把某物交给他人支配。

items.en: abandonen entered English with the sense of handing over or surrendering.
items.cn: abandonen 进入英语时意为交出、让与。

items.en: the sense shifted from surrendering to leaving something behind.
items.cn: 词义从「让与」转为「丢下不管」。

items.en: abandon now covers giving up plans, people and places.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖放弃计划、抛弃他人与遗弃地方。

items.en: the noun with abandon names a careless freedom.
items.cn: 名词搭配 with abandon 指一种无所拘束的自由。

note.en: The look-alike group is the abandon family; the near-meaning group is other verbs of leaving.
note.cn: 形近组是 abandon 词族；近义组是别的表示「离开、舍弃」的动词。

definition_zh: 使卑下；使谦卑；降低自己的身份
definition_en: to make someone or yourself seem lower in rank, status, or dignity
core_image: 一个人被按下头去，头顶的高度被一寸寸压低
scene: 颁奖礼上，昔日的主帅要在众人面前向新王行礼。The defeated general was forced to abase himself before the new king.
sceneCN: 这里 abase 是「使卑下、使谦卑」（第 2 个义项：主动降低自己的身份）；句意为战败的将军被迫在新王面前自贬行礼。

pos.zh: （常与反身代词连用）自贬；谦卑自己

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「屈辱；自贬；降位」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「被贬低的；屈辱的」
同根近义词，加 de- 构成，义为「贬低；贬值」

senses.title: To lower someone else's dignity
senses.definition: to lower the rank, honour, or dignity of another person, often by force or humiliation
senses.definitionCN: 压低另一个人的地位、荣誉或尊严，常通过强制或羞辱
senses.example: The tyrant abased his rivals in front of the whole court.
senses.exampleCN: 暴君在全朝廷面前羞辱贬抑他的对手。
senses.why: The low base of a building holds everything up; to abase is to push a person down to that low level.
senses.whyCN: 建筑物的 base 是最低的基座；abase 就是把人压到那个最低的高度。

senses.title: To lower oneself
senses.definition: to behave so as to lower one's own dignity or status, usually to show humility or to beg
senses.definitionCN: 以压低自己身份或地位的方式行事，通常为表示谦卑或乞求
senses.example: He abased himself and begged for the queen's forgiveness.
senses.exampleCN: 他自贬身份，乞求王后的宽恕。
senses.why: When no one else pushes, the person bends down alone; the reflexive use keeps the same downward motion with oneself as the object.
senses.whyCN: 没有别人施压时，人自己弯下身去；反身用法保持同一个向下的动作，只是对象换成了自己。

senses.title: To reduce the value or standing of a thing
senses.titleCN: 贬低事物的价值或地位
senses.definition: to lower the worth, quality, or standing of something abstract, such as a title or a currency
senses.definitionCN: 降低某抽象事物（如头衔、货币）的价值、品质或地位
senses.example: The endless scandals abased the office of mayor.
senses.exampleCN: 接连不断的丑闻贬损了市长这一职位。
senses.why: What works on persons extends to things; anything with standing or worth can be pressed down to a lower level.
senses.whyCN: 作用于人的动作延伸到事物上；凡有地位或价值者都可被压到更低的水准。

intro.en: Abase comes straight from the Old French abaisser, to lower, which was built on a Late Latin verb meaning to make low.
intro.cn: abase 直接来自古法语 abaisser「使降低」，后者建立在晚期拉丁语「使变低」的动词之上。

items.en: Bassiare meant to lower, formed on bassus, meaning low or short.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 bassiare 意为使降低，由 bassus「低的；矮的」构成。

items.en: Abaisser kept the same meaning: to bring down, to lower.
items.cn: 古法语 abaisser 保留了同一含义：使下降、使降低。

items.en: The verb spread with courtly and religious usage, describing bowing and humility.
items.cn: 中古法语动词随宫廷与宗教用语传播，描写鞠躬与谦卑。

items.en: English borrowed abase in the sixteenth century, first for lowering pride and rank.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪借入 abase，最早用于压低骄傲与地位。

items.en: Today it survives mainly in the reflexive phrase abase oneself.
items.cn: 如今该词主要存于反身短语 abase oneself 之中。

note.en: Abase shares its French family with abash, and its Latin base with abject.
note.cn: abase 与 abash 同属法语词族，又与 abject 共享拉丁语 base 词根。

normalIntro.en: The base inside the word gives five anchors for memory.

normal.en: a- + base: push someone down to the base level.
normal.cn: a-（去）＋ base（基座）：把人压到基座的高度。

normal.en: abasement is the noun: the state of being pushed low.
normal.cn: abasement 是名词：被压低的状态，即屈辱。

normal.en: debase lowers value; abase lowers dignity.

normal.en: abase oneself: you bend down by yourself.
normal.cn: abase oneself：自己弯下身去，自贬。

normal.en: Compare abash: shame in the face, not rank.
normal.cn: 对比 abash：那是脸红的窘迫，不是身份的贬低。

abstract.en: Picture an elevator that only goes down.
abstract.cn: 想象一部只能下行的电梯。

abstract.en: See a proud peacock pushed to a stone base.
abstract.cn: 看见一只骄傲的孔雀被按到石质基座上。

abstract.en: Feel the floor drop one rank lower.
abstract.cn: 感到脚下的地板又往下沉了一个等级。

examples.en: He abased himself to win back the king's favour.
examples.cn: 他自贬身份以赢回国王的宠爱。

examples.en: The cruel remarks were meant to abase her before her colleagues.
examples.cn: 那些刻薄的话意在使她在同事面前受辱。

examples.en: Such conduct abases the honour of the whole family.
examples.cn: 这种行为贬损了整个家族的名誉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「鹅卑视」——鹅被压得低下头，显出一副卑微的样子

root: 古法语 abaisser「使降低」＝ a-（源自拉丁 ad-）＋ baisser「使变低」，baisser 来自晚期拉丁语 bassiare，词根 bassus「低的」。与英语 base「基座」同源。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses move one downward motion: from pushing another down, to bending oneself, to cheapening a thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项共用同一个向下的动作：从压低别人，到自己弯腰，再到贬低事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person pushed down until the head is level with the base.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人被压下去，头与基座齐平。

branches.en: PUSHING DOWN ANOTHER: rank and honour are lowered by force.
branches.cn: 压低他人：地位与荣誉被强力压低。

branches.en: BENDING ONESELF: the same motion done alone as humility or begging.
branches.cn: 自己弯腰：同样的动作独自完成，出于谦卑或乞求。

branches.en: PRESSING A THING DOWN: worth and standing of abstract things sink.
branches.cn: 压低事物：抽象事物的价值与地位下沉。

branches.en: OUTSIDE FORCE: someone or something does the pressing.
branches.cn: 外力作用：由他者施压。

branches.en: ONE DOWNWARD LINE: every sense is a fall toward the base.
branches.cn: 同一条下行线：每个义项都是向基座的坠落。

intro.en: The word is French in shape, with one Latin root and one French prefix.
intro.cn: 这个词是法语形态：一个拉丁词根加一个法语前缀。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin bassiare is recorded, and bassus is attested, so the root is historical.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语 bassiare 有文献记录，bassus 亦见于记载，词根有史可查。

definition_zh: 使困窘；使羞愧；使局促不安
definition_en: to make someone feel embarrassed, ashamed, or uncomfortable
core_image: 一句当众戳破的话，让人的脸瞬间红透、手足无措
scene: 她在讨论会上被老师当众点名回答难题。The unexpected question abashed her in front of the whole class.
sceneCN: 这里 abash 是「使困窘」（第 1 个义项：令人当众难堪）；句意为一个出其不意的问题让她在全班面前局促不安。

pos.zh: 使局促不安（常用过去分词 abashed）

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转作形容词，义为「窘迫的；局促不安的」
加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不害臊的；毫不羞愧的」

senses.title: To embarrass someone
senses.definition: to make someone feel embarrassed or awkward, especially in public
senses.definitionCN: 使人感到尴尬或难堪，尤指当众
senses.example: The teacher's sudden praise abashed the shy student.
senses.exampleCN: 老师突如其来的表扬让害羞的学生窘迫起来。
senses.why: Old French esba- carried the idea of striking someone wide and open; a sudden blow to the face makes the cheeks burn.
senses.whyCN: 古法语词干带有「猛然打开放倒」的意味；突袭式的一击会让人脸上发烫。

senses.title: To shame someone into silence
senses.definition: to make a person feel so ashamed or small that they stop speaking or acting
senses.definitionCN: 使人感到羞愧或渺小，以致停止说话或行动
senses.example: Her cold logic abashed the loudest debater into silence.
senses.exampleCN: 她冷静的逻辑使那位最吵的辩手羞愧语塞。
senses.why: Shame presses the mouth shut; the embarrassment of the first sense deepens into a shame that ends the exchange.
senses.whyCN: 羞愧把嘴压上；第一义的尴尬加深为一种让交流终止的羞耻。

senses.title: To unsettle someone's composure
senses.definition: to disturb someone's confidence or composure, even without a public audience
senses.definitionCN: 扰乱某人的自信或镇定，即使并无旁观者
senses.example: The strange smile on the portrait abashed every visitor.
senses.exampleCN: 画像上那抹怪异的微笑使每位访客都心神不定。
senses.why: The same blow can land inside: confidence is knocked open and off balance, whether or not anyone is watching.
senses.whyCN: 同样的一击也可以落在心里：自信被击开、失衡，无论有无旁观者。

intro.en: Abash descends from an Anglo-French verb meaning to strike open or throw into confusion, built on a root meaning to gape.
intro.cn: abash 源自盎格鲁-法语动词「猛击使张口、使人混乱」，其词根意为「张大口」。

items.en: A Frankish root for gaping or yawning is reconstructed behind the French verb.
items.cn: 法语动词背后重构出一个法兰克语词根，意为张口、打哈欠。

items.en: Esbaer meant to gape in wonder or be struck open with astonishment.
items.cn: 古法语 esbaer 意为惊讶地张口，或被惊得敞开。

items.en: Abaiss-, used in England, took the sense of confounding or striking with shame.
items.cn: 在英格兰使用的盎格鲁-法语形式 abaisse 转指使人混乱、使人蒙羞。

items.en: Abashen appeared with the meaning to make ashamed.
items.cn: 中古英语 abashen 出现，意为使人羞愧。

items.en: The verb survives mostly in the participle abashed and its negative unabashed.
items.cn: 该动词如今主要存于分词 abashed 及其否定式 unabashed。

note.en: Abash is often confused with abase, though the two come from different French verbs.
note.cn: abash 常与 abase 混淆，二者虽词尾相近，却来自不同的法语动词。

entries.definition: to lower someone's dignity, not their composure
entries.definitionCN: 贬低某人的身份尊严，而非使其窘迫；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the participle meaning embarrassed

entries.definitionCN: 使人心神不安；语域更书面

normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手把 abash 和发烫的脸绑在一起。

normal.en: a- + bash: like being smacked, the face burns.
normal.cn: a- ＋ bash（像挨了一巴掌）：脸瞬间发烫。

normal.en: abashed describes the red-cheeked state.
normal.cn: abashed 形容两颊发红的状态。

normal.en: unabashed: not red at all, shameless and calm.
normal.cn: unabashed：毫不脸红，坦然自若。

normal.en: Contrast abase: rank goes down, only cheeks burn here.
normal.cn: 对比 abase：那边是身份下降，这边只是脸红。

normal.en: Think of bashful, a cousin feeling of shyness.
normal.cn: 联想 bashful「害羞的」，情绪近亲。

abstract.en: Picture a spotlight snapping on at a bad moment.
abstract.cn: 想象难堪时刻聚光灯骤然亮起。

abstract.en: Feel the floor vanish under a too-big applause.
abstract.cn: 感到掌声过大时脚下地板消失。

abstract.en: See mouths gaping open in one stunned room.
abstract.cn: 看见满屋人张口结舌的样子。

examples.en: Nothing could abash her once she decided to speak.
examples.cn: 一旦决定开口，什么都无法让她窘迫退缩。

examples.en: He stood abashed by his own careless words.
examples.cn: 他被自己无心的话弄得窘迫不已。

examples.en: The truth abashed the liar in front of the crowd.
examples.cn: 真相使说谎者在众人面前羞愧难当。

root: 一般认为源自古法语 esbaer「惊愕张口」＝ es-（出自拉丁 ex-「向外」）＋ baer「张大口」（日耳曼语源，与 gape 之源相关）。经盎格鲁-法语进入中古英语 abashen。词根部分属重构形式，学者意见不一。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses widen one blow: from public embarrassment to shaming silence to inner unrest.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项扩展同一次「击打」：从当众难堪，到羞得语塞，再到内心不安。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one sudden strike opens the face and the room stares.
core.cn: 核心意象：猛然一击，脸被打开，满屋目光落在上面。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC BLOW: embarrassment before an audience.
branches.cn: 当众一击：在旁观者面前的尴尬。

branches.en: THE DEEPENED BLOW: shame closes the mouth.
branches.cn: 加深的一击：羞愧让嘴闭上。

branches.en: THE INNER BLOW: composure shakes with no crowd needed.
branches.cn: 内心一击：无需观众，镇定也为之动摇。

branches.en: FACE BEFORE OTHERS: both senses need the eyes of others.
branches.cn: 人前的脸：这两个义项都依赖他人的目光。

branches.en: ONE STRIKE, THREE DEPTHS: skin, mouth, mind.
branches.cn: 一击三重：皮肤、嘴巴、心神。

intro.en: The frame is French with an ex- prefix, while the inner root is Germanic.
intro.cn: 框架是法语的，带 ex- 类前缀，而内部词根来自日耳曼语。

latinIntro.en: Latin ex- contributes the French es-, but the gaping root itself is a Germanic reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ex- 提供了法语 es-，但「张口」词根本身属日耳曼语重构形式。

它与 bash- 的情绪同族。

definition_zh: 减弱；减退；缓解；降低；废除
definition_en: to become less strong, intense, or numerous, or to make something less so
core_image: 正在退去的潮水：水位一点点往下落
scene: 暴雨敲了一整夜，天快亮时风声渐渐松了下来。By morning the storm had abated and the streets were quiet.
sceneCN: 这里 abate 是「强度减弱」（第 1 个义项：风暴等自然力量变弱）；句意为到早晨风暴已经减弱，街道安静下来。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「减弱；减免；废止」
由否定前缀加过去分词构成，义为「未减弱的；不减的」
由动词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「减轻者；消除者」

senses.title: Of a storm: to become weaker
senses.definition: of wind, rain, or a storm, to lose force
senses.definitionCN: 指风、雨或风暴失去力量
senses.example: The storm abated before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明前风暴减弱了。
senses.why: The Old French verb abatre meant 'to beat down'; a storm that is beaten down loses its force, and the image survives in every later use.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词 abatre 意为「打下去」；被压下去的风暴失去力量，这个意象一直留到后来的所有用法里。

senses.title: Of pain or fever: to subside
senses.definition: of pain, fever, or a symptom, to become less severe
senses.definitionCN: 指疼痛、发烧或症状变得不那么严重
senses.example: The fever abated after the medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 服药之后，发烧退了。
senses.why: Illness is pictured as a force pressing on the body; when that pressure is beaten down, the symptom subsides.
senses.whyCN: 疾病被想象成压在身体上的一股力量；这股压力被压下去，症状也就减轻了。

senses.title: Of anger: to cool down
senses.definition: of anger, excitement, or tension, to become calmer
senses.definitionCN: 指怒气、激动或紧张变得平静
senses.example: His anger abated once he heard the full story.
senses.exampleCN: 听完完整经过后，他的怒气平息了。
senses.why: Emotions rise like weather; the same verb that describes a dying storm describes a temper losing its heat.
senses.whyCN: 情绪像天气一样升起；描述风暴渐息的那个动词，也同样描述脾气退热。

senses.title: Of numbers: to decrease
senses.definition: to fall in amount, rate, or number
senses.definitionCN: 在数量、比率或数目上下降
senses.example: Inflation showed no sign of abating.
senses.exampleCN: 通胀没有任何减弱的迹象。
senses.why: From wind and fever the word extends to anything measurable that rises too high and then comes down.
senses.whyCN: 从风与发烧，这个词扩展到任何升得过高、随后回落的可测量事物。

senses.title: To reduce a charge
senses.definition: to make a rent, tax, or charge smaller
senses.definitionCN: 使租金、税款或费用变少
senses.example: The landlord agreed to abate the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 房东同意减免租金。
senses.why: A charge is a burden laid on someone; abating it is beating that burden down to a lighter weight.
senses.whyCN: 费用是压在某人身上的负担；abate 就是把这副担子打下去、减轻重量。

senses.title: Legal: to remove a nuisance
senses.definition: to end or remove a nuisance, especially by legal order
senses.definitionCN: 终止或消除妨害，尤指依法律命令
senses.example: The court ordered the factory to abate the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 法院命令工厂消除噪音。
senses.why: A nuisance is a harm that keeps pressing on a neighbourhood; the law uses the old beating image to say that the harm must be pushed down.
senses.whyCN: 妨害是持续压在社区上的一种损害；法律借用古老的「打压」意象，表示必须把这股损害压下去。

senses.title: Legal: to quash a writ
senses.definition: to render a legal writ or action void
senses.definitionCN: 使某项令状或法律诉讼失效
senses.example: The writ was abated when the defendant died.
senses.exampleCN: 被告死亡后，令状被废止。
senses.why: In law the image turns administrative: an action that can no longer stand is beaten down and declared void.
senses.whyCN: 在法律里，这个意象转为程序性的：无法继续的诉讼被压下去，宣告失效。

senses.title: To lessen something
senses.definition: to make pressure, risk, or intensity less
senses.definitionCN: 使压力、风险或强度变小
senses.example: The new policy abated the pressure on hospitals.
senses.exampleCN: 新政策减轻了医院的压力。
senses.why: The transitive use simply puts the same beating action into someone's hands: an agent lowers the force instead of waiting for it to fall.
senses.whyCN: 及物用法只是把同样的「打压」动作交到某人手里：由人主动降低力量，而不是等它自己落下。

intro.en: Abate comes from a French verb meaning 'to beat down', which goes back to the Latin verb for beating.
intro.cn: abate 来自一个意为「打下去」的法语动词，后者可追溯到表示「打」的拉丁语动词。

items.en: battuere meant 'to beat, strike'; it also lies behind English battle and battery.
items.cn: battuere 意为「打、击」，英语 battle 与 battery 也源自它。

items.en: A reconstructed compound of ad- 'to' and battuere gave the sense 'to beat down'; the form is reconstructed, not attested.
items.cn: 由 ad-（向）与 battuere 构成的重构词，得到「打下去」之义；这一形式是重构的，并非实际文献所载。

items.en: abatre meant 'to knock down, fell, destroy', and its figurative sense 'to lessen' was already present.
items.cn: abatre 意为「击倒、砍倒、摧毁」，其比喻义「减弱」当时已经存在。

items.en: English abaten is recorded from the fourteenth century with the sense 'to diminish'.
items.cn: 英语 abaten 自十四世纪有记录，意为「减少、减弱」。

items.en: Medical and legal senses were added later, including the abatement of a nuisance or a writ.
items.cn: 医学与法律义项是后来增加的，包括消除妨害与废止令状。

note.en: The first group gathers words sharing the Latin verb for beating; the second gathers verbs for things becoming smaller or weaker.
note.cn: 第一组收共享拉丁语「打」这一动词的词；第二组收表示事物变小变弱的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for a reduction in strength, amount, or a legal charge.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「减弱、减少、减免」，指强度、数量或费用的降低。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning that something continues without any reduction.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「未减弱的」，表示某事毫无减弱地持续。

entries.definition: A partial refund; it comes from the same French verb for beating something back.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「折扣、退款」，同样来自那个表示「打回去」的法语动词。

entries.definition: A set of connected cells, or the act of beating; both go back to Latin battuere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电池组」或「殴打」，二者都可追溯到拉丁语 battuere。

entries.definition: A formal discussion; it shares the beating root through the idea of striking words together.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「辩论」，经由「话语交锋」的观念共享同一个「打」的词根。

entries.definition: Of a storm, flood, or feeling, to sink to a lower level.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「平息、退去」，指风暴、洪水或情绪降到较低水平。

entries.definition: To become or make smaller in size, amount, or importance.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「减少、缩小」，指在大小、数量或重要性上变小。

entries.definition: To reduce in degree or extent.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「减轻、减少」，指在程度或范围上降低。

entries.definition: To become gradually smaller or weaker over time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「逐渐减少」，指随时间慢慢变小或变弱。

entries.definition: Of tides or energy, to flow back and decline.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「退潮、衰退」，指潮水或精力退回、减弱。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the legal collocation, the storm image, and the noun family; the abstract hooks turn the falling water level into three pictures.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用法律搭配、风暴意象与名词词族；抽象记忆点把下落的水位化成三幅画面。

normal.en: Abate a nuisance is a standard legal phrase for removing a harmful condition.
normal.cn: abate a nuisance 是标准法律短语，表示消除有害状况。

normal.en: A storm abates; the same verb appears in weather reports and in news about inflation.
normal.cn: 风暴会 abate；同一个动词也出现在天气播报和通胀新闻里。

normal.en: Unabated means the force never dropped, as in 'the storm continued unabated'.
normal.cn: unabated 表示力量从未下降，如「风暴持续不减」。

normal.en: Abatement is the noun, common in rent abatement and noise abatement.
normal.cn: 名词 abatement 常见于减租与降噪的说法中。

normal.en: The -ate ending marks a verb, and the French source verb meant to beat down.
normal.cn: -ate 结尾标明动词，法语来源动词意为「打下去」。

abstract.en: Picture a tide pulling back from a stone pier, leaving the steps dry.
abstract.cn: 想象潮水从石码头退去，把台阶留在干燥处。

abstract.en: Picture a flame turned down by a knob until it is only a blue ring.
abstract.cn: 想象火焰被旋钮调小，只剩一圈蓝光。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd's noise thinning out until the hall is almost silent.
abstract.cn: 想象人群的喧闹渐渐稀疏，直到大厅几乎无声。

examples.en: The wind abated just after sunset.
examples.cn: 日落之后风就减弱了。

examples.en: Nothing could abate her grief.
examples.cn: 什么都无法减轻她的悲伤。

examples.en: The council moved to abate noise from the highway.
examples.cn: 市议会着手降低高速公路的噪音。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额贝特」——像把音量键往下拨，额度一格格变小，声音就轻了。

root: 古法语 abatre（击倒、打下去），源自拉丁语 battuere（打）+ ad-（向）；核心义是「把力量打下去」

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from physical forces losing strength, through body and emotion, to measurable amounts and to legal actions that are cancelled.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从自然力量失去强度，经过身体与情绪，走到可计量的数量，最后是被撤销的法律行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: floodwater dropping down the marked steps of a pier
core.cn: 核心意象：洪水沿着码头刻度的台阶一层层退落

branches.en: Natural and bodily pressure falls away: storm, fever, and anger all lose heat.
branches.cn: 自然与身体的压力退去：风暴、发烧与怒气都失去热度。

branches.en: Measurable quantities fall: rates, numbers, and levels come down.
branches.cn: 可计量的数量下降：比率、数目与水平回落。

branches.en: A burden is made lighter by an agent: charges are cut and pressure is eased.
branches.cn: 人主动减轻负担：费用被减免，压力被缓解。

branches.en: A harmful condition is removed by legal order.
branches.cn: 依法律命令消除有害状况。

branches.en: A legal action is cancelled and declared void.
branches.cn: 法律行为被撤销并宣告失效。

intro.en: The family is held together by the French stem bat- 'to beat', with prefixes and suffixes that mark negation, result, and agent.
intro.cn: 这个词族由法语词干 bat-（打）连在一起，前缀与后缀分别标记否定、结果与施动者。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source verb battuere also produced battle, battery, and combat, so the Latin entries record the shared root rather than a direct ancestor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源动词 battuere 还生出 battle、battery、combat，因此拉丁条目记录的是共享词根，而非直接祖先。

items.meaning: present tense with he, she, or it

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「减弱；减免；废止」
形容词，义为「未减弱的；不减的」

definition_zh: 女修道院院长；尼姑庵住持
definition_en: a woman who is the head of a convent of nuns
core_image: 高墙修道院里，一位手持权杖、走在修女最前面的女性长者
scene: 晨钟响起，修女们在长廊列队等候。The abbess led the silent procession into the chapel.
sceneCN: 这里 abbess 是「女修道院院长」（第 1 个义项：女修道团体的首领）；句意为女院长领着安静的队列走进礼拜堂。

pos.zh: 女修道院院长（女修道团体的首领）

derivatives.zh: 同族男性形式，义为「男修道院院长」
同根名词，义为「修道院；大寺院」
由 abbot 加形容词后缀构成，义为「修道院长的」

senses.title: Head of a convent of nuns
senses.definition: the woman elected to govern a community of nuns and answer for its discipline and property
senses.definitionCN: 被推选管理修女团体、对其纪律与财产负责的女性
senses.example: The abbess signed the deed that granted the village its well.
senses.exampleCN: 女院长在授予该村水井的契据上签了字。
senses.why: A Syrian word for spiritual father crossed into Latin; adding the feminine ending turns the father into the mother of the house.
senses.whyCN: 一个叙利亚语的「属灵之父」传入拉丁语；加上阴性词尾，家父便成了女修道院的母亲。

senses.title: Female superior in religious life generally
senses.titleCN: 隐修女团的领导者（泛称）
senses.definition: any woman who holds the corresponding office of spiritual leadership over a female monastic community
senses.definitionCN: 泛指在女性隐修团体中担任相应属灵领袖职分的女性
senses.example: In old chronicles every abbess is listed with the year she took office.
senses.exampleCN: 在古老编年史中，每位女院长都记有就任年份。
senses.why: The office outlives any single building; wherever nuns gather under a rule, the word names the one who keeps it.
senses.whyCN: 这一职分超越了任何一座建筑；凡有修女依会规聚集之处，这个词就指维持会规的那个人。

intro.en: Abbess is the Latin feminine of abbot, a title that travelled from Syria through Greek and Latin into English.
intro.cn: abbess 是 abbot 的拉丁阴性形式，这一头衔经叙利亚语、希腊语和拉丁语传入英语。

items.en: Abba meant father, the address given to respected spiritual teachers.
items.cn: 叙利亚语 abba 意为父亲，是对受尊敬的属灵导师的称呼。

items.en: Abbas passed into Greek as a title for monastic elders.
items.cn: 希腊语 abbas 作为修道长者的称号传入。

items.en: Abbas became the formal title of the head of a monastery.
items.cn: 拉丁语 abbas 成为修道院院长的正式称号。

items.en: Abbesse was formed with a feminine ending and entered English as abbess.
items.cn: 古法语加阴性词尾构成 abbesse，进入英语成为 abbess。

items.en: The word names the head of a convent of nuns.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词指女修道院院长。

note.en: The word sits inside a small family: abbot, abbey, and its own feminine ending.
note.cn: 该词属于一个小词族：abbot、abbey 及其阴性词尾。

entries.definition: the male head of a monastery
entries.definitionCN: 男修道院院长；abbess 的男性对应形式

entries.definition: the building or community itself
entries.definitionCN: 修道院建筑或团体；同出 abba 词根

entries.definition: relating to an abbot or abbess
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「修道院长的」

entries.definition: the head of a priory of nuns
entries.definitionCN: 小修道院（priory）的女院长；层级略低

entries.definition: the head of some religious orders of women
entries.definitionCN: 某些女修会的负责人称谓

entries.definition: a general title for head of a religious house
entries.definitionCN: 修会负责人的通称

normalIntro.en: The abb- family offers five quick anchors.
normalIntro.cn: abb- 词族提供五个快速记忆抓手。

normal.en: abbess = abbot + ess, the female form.
normal.cn: abbess ＝ abbot ＋ ess，阴性形式。

normal.en: -ess marks women: actress, princess, abbess.
normal.cn: -ess 标记女性：actress、princess、abbess。

normal.en: abbey is the building; abbot or abbess leads it.
normal.cn: abbey 是建筑；abbot 或 abbess 是其首领。

normal.en: Double b remembers the Syrian abba, father.
normal.cn: 双写 b 提示叙利亚语 abba「父亲」。

normal.en: Pair it with abbot to fix the gender ending.
normal.cn: 与 abbot 配对记忆阴性词尾。

abstract.en: See a ring of keys at a black-robed waist.
abstract.cn: 想象黑袍腰间的一串钥匙。

abstract.en: Hear one bell that the whole convent obeys.
abstract.cn: 听一声全院遵从的钟。

abstract.en: Picture a seat slightly higher in the chapel.
abstract.cn: 想象礼拜堂里略高一级的座位。

examples.en: The abbess welcomed two new novices last spring.
examples.cn: 去年春天女院长接纳了两名新见习修女。

examples.en: Visitors were received in the hall beneath the abbess's window.
examples.cn: 访客在女院长窗下的厅堂受到接待。

examples.en: An abbess of great learning governed the convent for forty years.
examples.cn: 一位极有学问的女院长执掌这座修道院四十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿贝斯」——阿贝嬷嬷是院里说一不二的女当家

root: 叙利亚语 abba「父亲」→ 希腊语 abbas → 拉丁语 abbas「男修道院院长」；古法语加阴性词尾 abbesse，约十四世纪进入英语作 abbess。阴性后缀 -ess 出自拉丁语 -issa。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses share one office: the elected head of nuns, and the same leadership named generally.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项同属一个职分：被推选的修女首领，及其泛称用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mother of a house of nuns, keys and staff in hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座修女院的母亲，手持钥匙与权杖。

branches.en: THE OFFICE ITSELF: one elected woman governs the convent.
branches.cn: 职分本身：一位被推选的女性治理修道院。

branches.en: THE OFFICE IN RECORDS: the title marks leadership wherever nuns live under a rule.
branches.cn: 记载中的职分：凡有修女依规而居，此称号即指其领袖。

branches.en: THE FEMININE PAIR: both senses stand opposite abbot.
branches.cn: 阴性对应：两个义项都与 abbot 相对。

branches.en: AUTHORITY WITHIN WALLS: both are powers inside the enclosure.
branches.cn: 墙内权威：两者都是院墙之内的权力。

branches.en: ONE TITLE, TWO USES: specific head, then general superior.
branches.cn: 一名两用：从具体院长到泛称领袖。

intro.en: The word is a borrowed title with one feminine suffix added in French.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个借来的头衔，法语中加了一个阴性后缀。

latinIntro.en: Syriac abba and Latin abbas are both recorded, so the line of descent is historical.
latinIntro.cn: 叙利亚语 abba 与拉丁语 abbas 均有记载，承传脉络有史可查。

items.example: It began as an address to spiritual teachers.
items.exampleCN: 它起初是对属灵导师的称呼。

items.example: It is the English masculine form.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语中的阳性形式。

items.example: It forms abbess and actress alike.
items.exampleCN: 它同样构成 abbess 与 actress。

items.example: It comes from the same title for the place.
items.exampleCN: 它由同一称号转指场所。

derivatives.zh: 同族阳性名词，义为「男修道院院长」
同根名词，义为「修道院」

definition_zh: 大修道院；大寺院；修道院全体成员
definition_en: a large building or community of monks or nuns ruled by an abbot or abbess
core_image: 高墙与钟楼围出的修道院建筑群，晨钟在塔间回荡
scene: 山谷尽头，石墙和尖塔在雾里显出轮廓。The monks returned to the abbey before the evening bell.
sceneCN: 这里 abbey 是「大修道院」（第 1 个义项：修士或修女的建筑与团体）；句意为修士们在晚钟前回到修道院。

pos.zh: 修道院全体修士或修女（团体）

collocations.zh: 威斯敏斯特大教堂（西敏寺）

derivatives.zh: 同族名词，义为「男修道院院长」
同族名词，义为「女修道院院长」
由 abbot 加 -al 构成，义为「修道院长的」

senses.title: A monastic building complex
senses.definition: a group of buildings, with a church, where monks or nuns live and worship under an abbot or abbess
senses.definitionCN: 修士或修女在院长管辖下居住、礼拜的建筑群，含教堂
senses.example: The abbey owned the fields, the mill, and the bridge over the river.
senses.exampleCN: 这座修道院拥有田地、磨坊和河上的桥。
senses.why: The title of the head was turned into the name of the place he governed; the father's house became the abbey.
senses.whyCN: 首领的头衔被转用来指他治理的场所；属灵之父的房子就成了修道院。

senses.title: The community itself
senses.definition: the monks or nuns of such an establishment, taken as one body
senses.definitionCN: 指该机构中的修士或修女整体
senses.example: The whole abbey gathered in the chapter house at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时分全院成员聚集在议事厅。
senses.why: A building that holds one rule-bound family can be named for the family as well; walls and people share the word.
senses.whyCN: 容纳一个守规大家庭的建筑也可以用这个家庭命名；墙与人共用这个词。

senses.title: A former abbey kept as a church or landmark
senses.titleCN: 改建或残存的修道院建筑
senses.definition: a building that was once an abbey and now serves as a church, school, or historic site
senses.definitionCN: 原为修道院、如今用作教堂、学校或古迹的建筑
senses.example: Tourists cross the nave of the old abbey every afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 游客们每天下午穿过那座旧修道院的中殿。
senses.why: When the community dissolved, the name stayed with the stones; the label outlived the office.
senses.whyCN: 团体解散后，名字留在了石头上；名称比职分活得更久。

intro.en: Abbey began as the title of one man, Latin abbas, and grew into the name of the whole place he ruled.
intro.cn: abbey 原是一个人的头衔（拉丁语 abbas），后来扩展成他所治理的整个场所之名。

items.en: Abba, father, was the address for honoured spiritual teachers.
items.cn: 叙利亚语 abba「父亲」，是对受尊崇的属灵导师的称呼。

items.en: Abbas named the head of a monastery in both languages.
items.cn: 在希腊语与拉丁语中，abbas 指修道院院长。

items.en: Abee or abeie meant both the abbot's office and his house.
items.cn: 古法语 abee 或 abeie 既指院长之职，也指其宅邸。

items.en: Abbey entered English covering the buildings and the community.
items.cn: 中古英语 abbey 涵盖建筑与团体两层含义。

items.en: The word now names great monastic churches like Westminster Abbey.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词指大型修道院教堂，如威斯敏斯特大教堂。

note.en: Abbey belongs with abbot and abbess; nearby church words differ in origin.
note.cn: abbey 与 abbot、abbess 同族；邻近的教堂类词则来源不同。

entries.definition: the male head who rules the abbey
entries.definitionCN: 治理修道院的男院长；同出 abba 词根

entries.definition: the female head of a convent
entries.definitionCN: 女修道院院长；同根阴性形式

entries.definition: adjective relating to an abbot
entries.definitionCN: 与修道院长有关的形容词

entries.definition: a building where monks live
entries.definitionCN: 修士的居所；不强调院长头衔

entries.definition: a building where nuns live
entries.definitionCN: 修女的居所；与 abbey 相对应

entries.definition: a chief church of a bishop
entries.definitionCN: 主教座堂；由主教而非院长主持，词源不同

normalIntro.en: The abb- family plus place words give five anchors.
normalIntro.cn: abb- 词族加上场所联想给出五个抓手。

normal.en: abbey = the abbot's whole house.
normal.cn: abbey ＝ abbot 的整座宅邸。

normal.en: abba means father; the abbey is the father's house.
normal.cn: abba 意为父亲；abbey 是父亲的家。

normal.en: Westminster Abbey is the most famous example.
normal.cn: 威斯敏斯特大教堂是最著名的例子。

normal.en: Monks or nuns: either community can be an abbey.
normal.cn: 修士或修女团体都可称 abbey。

normal.en: -ey sounds like many place endings in English.
normal.cn: -ey 的读音类似英语常见的地名后缀。

abstract.en: Hear one bell rolling over cloister walls.
abstract.cn: 听一声钟声漫过回廊高墙。

abstract.en: See candle rows in a wide stone nave.
abstract.cn: 看见宽阔石殿里成排的烛光。

abstract.en: Smell old paper and cold incense.
abstract.cn: 闻到旧纸张与冷香的气味。

examples.en: The abbey was founded in the twelfth century.
examples.cn: 这座修道院建于十二世纪。

examples.en: Kings were crowned in the abbey for centuries.
examples.cn: 数个世纪以来，国王们都在这座大教堂加冕。

examples.en: Rain fell on the grey roofs of the abbey.
examples.cn: 雨落在修道院灰色的屋顶上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿贝」——阿贝一家住进高墙石殿，成了清修的大家族

root: 叙利亚语 abba「父亲」→ 希腊语／拉丁语 abbas「修道院长」→ 晚期拉丁语 abbatia「院长之职／院长宅邸」→ 古法语 abeie → 中古英语 abbey。由「职位」引申为「场所」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses grow one title outward: the buildings, the people, and the stones left behind.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项由一个头衔向外生长：建筑、人群、以及遗存的石头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walled father's house of prayer, bell tower at the centre.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座有围墙的祈祷之家，中央立着钟楼。

branches.en: THE WALLS: church, cloister, mill and fields under one rule.
branches.cn: 墙：教堂、回廊、磨坊与田地同归一个会规。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: the community gathered as one body.
branches.cn: 人：作为一个整体聚集的团体。

branches.en: THE REMAINS: the name stays with the stones after the office ends.
branches.cn: 遗存：职分结束后名字仍留在石头上。

branches.en: PLACE WORDS: both senses name buildings rather than persons.
branches.cn: 场所义：这两个义项都指建筑而非人。

branches.en: ONE TITLE OUTWARD: office to house to people to ruin.
branches.cn: 一个头衔的外扩：职分→宅邸→团体→遗迹。

intro.en: One Syrian root runs through the whole family; English adds only place use.
intro.cn: 一个叙利亚语词根贯穿整个词族；英语只是增加了场所用法。

latinIntro.en: Latin abbas and abbatia are recorded forms, so the chain is historical.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abbas 与 abbatia 均为有记载的形式，链条有史可查。

items.example: It is the first form of the title.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一头衔的最初形式。

definition_zh: 退位；正式放弃（权力、职责）
definition_en: to give up a throne, power, or duty in an official or formal way
core_image: 王座上的人摘下王冠，轻轻放在空出的座位上
scene: 宫墙内外议论纷纷，人们仰望着阳台上那个身影。The ageing king announced that he would abdicate in favour of his son.
sceneCN: 这里 abdicate 是「退位」（第 1 个义项：正式让出王位）；句意为年迈的国王宣布将把王位让给儿子。

pos.zh: 正式放弃（权力、职责、王位）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「退位；正式放弃」
由动词加 -able 构成，义为「可放弃的」

senses.title: To give up a throne
senses.definition: to formally give up the office of king, queen, or emperor
senses.definitionCN: 正式放弃国王、女王或皇帝的职位
senses.example: The emperor abdicated after the revolution and left for exile.
senses.exampleCN: 革命之后皇帝退位，流亡他乡。
senses.why: The Latin prefix ab- means away and dicare means to proclaim; to abdicate is to proclaim oneself away from the throne.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁前缀 ab- 表示离开，dicare 意为宣告；abdicate 就是宣告自己离开王座。

senses.title: To formally give up power or office
senses.definition: to formally surrender authority or an official position
senses.definitionCN: 正式交出权威或官职
senses.example: The general abdicated his command before the inquiry began.
senses.exampleCN: 调查开始前，将军正式交出了指挥权。
senses.why: What works for one throne works for any seat of power; the same public renouncing applies to offices.
senses.whyCN: 适用于王座的动作同样适用于任何权力之座；同样的公开弃绝适用于各种职位。

senses.title: To fail one's duty
senses.definition: to neglect or refuse a duty that one is expected to carry out
senses.definitionCN: 疏忽或拒绝承担本应履行的职责
senses.example: Parents who never set limits abdicate their responsibility.
senses.exampleCN: 从不设限的父母就是在推卸自己的责任。
senses.why: A duty is also a seat one should keep; to abandon the duty is to leave that seat empty.
senses.whyCN: 职责也是一个人应当坐守的位子；弃置职责就是让那个位子空着。

intro.en: Abdicate is Latin in the open: ab-, away, plus dicare, to proclaim; the word literally says one declares oneself apart from the seat.
intro.cn: abdicate 是明明白白的拉丁语：ab-「离开」加 dicare「宣告」；这个词字面意思就是宣告自己离开那个位子。

items.en: The root deik- meant to show or point out, the ancestor of dicare.
items.cn: 原始印欧词根 deik- 意为指示、指出，是 dicare 的祖先。

items.en: Abdicare meant to renounce or disown, formally declaring away.
items.cn: 拉丁语 abdicare 意为公开弃绝、声明脱离。

items.en: In Roman law it covered renouncing office, family ties, and property claims.
items.cn: 在罗马法中，它涵盖放弃官职、家庭关系与财产主张。

items.en: English took abdicate in the seventeenth century, first about office and duty.
items.cn: 英语于十七世纪借入 abdicate，最初指官职与职责。

items.en: After famous royal abdications, the throne sense became the most familiar.
items.cn: 几桩著名的王室退位事件之后，「退位」义项最为人熟知。

note.en: Abdicate shares its dic- root with words about saying and pointing.
note.cn: abdicate 的 dic- 词根与一批表示「说、指」的词同族。

entries.definition: the noun meaning a formal giving up
entries.definitionCN: 名词形式，义为退位、正式放弃

entries.definition: to devote something to a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 奉献；与 abdicate 同根而方向相反，由 de- 构成

entries.definition: to point out or show
entries.definitionCN: 指出；同根 dicare 的普通用法

entries.definition: to give up a job or post
entries.definitionCN: 辞职、放弃职位；语域更日常

entries.definition: to declare one gives up a claim or right
entries.definitionCN: 声明放弃权利或主张

entries.definition: to let go of something held
entries.definitionCN: 放手交出所持之物

normalIntro.en: Five anchors tie abdicate to leaving a declared seat.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手把 abdicate 与「宣告离开位子」绑在一起。

normal.en: ab- away + dic- proclaim: proclaim oneself away.
normal.cn: ab-（离开）＋ dic-（宣告）：宣告自己离开。

normal.en: abdication is the noun for the formal act.
normal.cn: abdication 是这一正式行为的名词。

normal.en: dedicate goes the other way: hand oneself in.
normal.cn: dedicate 方向相反：把自己交进去。

normal.en: abdicate responsibility: leave the duty-seat empty.
normal.cn: abdicate responsibility：让职责之座空着。

normal.en: Remember the famous 1936 royal abdication.
normal.cn: 记住 1936 年著名的王室退位事件。

abstract.en: Picture a crown set gently on an empty throne.
abstract.cn: 想象王冠被轻轻放在空王座上。

abstract.en: Hear a herald reading a renunciation aloud.
abstract.cn: 听传令官高声宣读退位文告。

abstract.en: Feel the sceptre slide through open fingers.
abstract.cn: 感到权杖从张开的手指间滑落。

examples.en: The king chose to abdicate rather than sign the decree.
examples.cn: 国王宁可退位也不签署那道法令。

examples.en: By ignoring the reports, the board abdicated its duty of care.
examples.cn: 董事会无视报告，等于放弃了它的审慎职责。

examples.en: She abdicated the chairmanship after twenty years.
examples.cn: 二十年后她卸任了主席一职。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我不替戴」——王冠我不替你戴了，你自己摘下来

root: 拉丁语 abdicare ＝ ab-「离开」＋ dicare「宣告」；dicare 出自原始印欧词根 deik-「指示」。罗马法中指正式弃绝，十七世纪进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses keep the public renouncing: a throne, an office, and a duty.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项保持同一种公开弃绝：王座、官职、职责。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crown lifted off and a seat left empty by proclamation.
core.cn: 核心意象：王冠被摘下，座位于宣告声中空出。

branches.en: THE THRONE: the highest seat is publicly left.
branches.cn: 王座：最高的位子被公开离开。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: command and authority change hands by the same act.
branches.cn: 官职：同一动作让指挥权与权威易手。

branches.en: THE DUTY: the empty seat is one that should have been kept.
branches.cn: 职责：空出的位子本应有人坐守。

branches.en: FORMAL RENOUNCING: both senses need an official declaration.
branches.cn: 正式弃绝：这两个义项都需要正式宣告。

branches.en: ONE LEAVING: every sense is a step away from a seat.
branches.cn: 同一种离开：每个义项都是离开一个位子的那一步。

intro.en: The word is a transparent Latin compound, prefix and verb root both intact.
intro.cn: 这个词是透明的拉丁复合词：前缀与动词词根都完好保留。

latinIntro.en: Latin abdicare and its legal use are recorded in classical sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abdicare 及其法律用法见于古典文献。

items.example: It is the reconstructed ancestor of dicare.
items.exampleCN: 它是 dicare 的重构祖先形式。

items.example: It shows the root's positive direction.
items.exampleCN: 它展示词根的正面方向。
它是 dic- 的另一个后裔。

items.example: It is a famous dic- descendant.
items.exampleCN: 它是 dic- 词根的著名后裔。

definition_zh: 腹部；腹腔；（昆虫、甲壳类的）腹部
definition_en: the part of the body between the chest and the pelvis, or the rear section of an insect's or crustacean's body
core_image: 躯干中段那个装着肠胃的柔软腔体
scene: 医生先让病人平躺，再轻轻按压腹部寻找痛点。The surgeon pressed gently on her abdomen to locate the source of the pain.
sceneCN: 这里 abdomen 是「腹部」（第 1 个义项：人体胸部与骨盆之间的区域）；句意为外科医生轻按她的腹部，寻找疼痛的来源。

pos.zh: 昆虫或甲壳动物的腹部体段

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「腹部的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「在腹部；按腹部方式」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「大腹的；肥胖的」
由本词与表示「成形术」的成分构成，义为「腹壁整形术」

senses.title: The human belly region
senses.definition: the front part of the body between the chest and the hips, containing the stomach and intestines
senses.definitionCN: 人体胸部与髋部之间的前部区域，内有胃与肠
senses.example: He felt a sharp pain in his abdomen after dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭后他感到腹部一阵剧痛。
senses.why: Latin abdomen named the belly as a whole; the word entered medical English as the neutral term for the region that holds the digestive organs.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abdomen 整体指「肚子」；这个词作为中性术语进入医学英语，指容纳消化器官的区域。

senses.title: The abdominal cavity
senses.definition: the space inside the body that contains the stomach, intestines, liver, and other organs
senses.definitionCN: 体内容纳胃、肠、肝等器官的空间
senses.example: The scan showed fluid in the abdomen.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示腹腔内有积液。
senses.why: Once the outer belly is named, the same word is extended inward to the cavity behind it.
senses.whyCN: 外部腹部有了名称之后，同一个词又被向内延伸到它后面的腔体。

senses.title: The insect abdomen
senses.definition: the third and rear section of an insect's body, behind the thorax
senses.definitionCN: 昆虫身体第三节，位于胸部之后
senses.example: The wasp's sting sits at the tip of its abdomen.
senses.exampleCN: 黄蜂的刺长在腹部的末端。
senses.why: Entomology borrowed the human term for the rear body segment because it also holds the gut.
senses.whyCN: 昆虫学借用了人体术语来指后部体段，因为那里同样容纳肠道。

senses.title: The crustacean abdomen
senses.definition: the segmented rear part of a crustacean such as a shrimp or crab
senses.definitionCN: 虾或蟹等甲壳动物分节的躯干后部
senses.example: The shrimp flexed its abdomen to propel itself backward.
senses.exampleCN: 虾弯曲腹部，把自己向后推。
senses.why: In arthropods the same body plan repeats, so the belly word naturally covers the tail-like rear section.
senses.whyCN: 节肢动物的身体结构彼此相似，因此这个「肚子」的词自然也能指像尾巴一样的后段。

senses.title: The arachnid abdomen
senses.definition: the rear body part of a spider or similar animal, which contains the digestive and reproductive organs
senses.definitionCN: 蜘蛛等动物躯干的后部，内含消化与生殖器官
senses.example: The spider's abdomen is often larger than its front body.
senses.exampleCN: 蜘蛛的腹部往往比前体更大。
senses.why: The term is a general anatomical label for the hind body, whatever the species.
senses.whyCN: 这个术语是所有物种后部躯体的通用解剖标签。

senses.title: A paunch
senses.definition: a rounded or fat belly, used in everyday speech
senses.definitionCN: 日常口语中指圆鼓或肥胖的肚子
senses.example: He patted his abdomen and laughed about his diet.
senses.exampleCN: 他拍拍自己的肚腩，笑谈起节食。
senses.why: The neutral medical word is softened into a friendly or teasing reference to a large belly.
senses.whyCN: 中性的医学词被软化，用来友善或打趣地指肥大的肚子。

senses.title: Acute abdomen
senses.definition: a medical condition of sudden severe abdominal pain that may need surgery
senses.definitionCN: 突发剧烈腹痛、可能需要手术的医学状况
senses.example: The patient was admitted with an acute abdomen.
senses.exampleCN: 病人因急腹症入院。
senses.why: A body region becomes a clinical label: the abdomen itself signals the emergency.
senses.whyCN: 一个身体区域变成了临床标签：腹部本身就在提示急症。

senses.title: The lower trunk of a vertebrate
senses.definition: the lower trunk region of a vertebrate animal, between the rib cage and the pelvis
senses.definitionCN: 脊椎动物肋骨与骨盆之间的躯干下部区域
senses.example: The frog's abdomen is pale and smooth.
senses.exampleCN: 青蛙的腹部苍白而光滑。
senses.why: Comparative anatomy uses the same term across vertebrates, keeping the meaning close to the original Latin belly.
senses.whyCN: 比较解剖学在各类脊椎动物中沿用同一个词，含义贴近拉丁语原义「肚子」。

intro.en: Abdomen is a Latin anatomical word of uncertain origin; it may be linked to the verb 'to hide', because the belly hides the organs.
intro.cn: abdomen 是一个来源不确定的拉丁语解剖词；它可能与表示「藏起来」的动词有关，因为肚子把器官藏在里面。

items.en: No agreed Indo-European root has been reconstructed for abdomen; the deeper history of the word is source uncertain.
items.cn: abdomen 尚无可公认的原始印欧语词根；这个词更深层的来源不确定。

items.en: Latin abdomen meant 'belly'. One common suggestion links it to abdere 'to hide', but this is a hypothesis, not an established fact.
items.cn: 拉丁语 abdomen 意为「肚子」。一种常见推测把它与 abdere（藏起来）联系起来，但这只是假说，并非定论。

items.en: The adjective abdominalis already existed in Latin medical writing.
items.cn: 形容词 abdominalis 在拉丁医学文献中已经存在。

items.en: French medical texts adopted abdomen in the sixteenth century as a learned term.
items.cn: 十六世纪的法语医学文献把这个词作为学术术语吸收进来。

items.en: English anatomy books took the word from Latin and French, keeping its neutral clinical tone.
items.cn: 英语解剖学著作从拉丁语和法语借入该词，保留了它中性、临床的语气。

items.en: Later biology extended it to insects and crustaceans, whose rear body segment is also called the abdomen.
items.cn: 后来的生物学把它扩展到昆虫与甲壳动物，它们后部的体段同样称作腹部。

note.en: The first group gathers the adjective and related medical forms; the second gathers everyday words for the belly.
note.cn: 第一组收形容词与相关医学形式；第二组收日常表示肚子的词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of or relating to the abdomen'.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「腹部的；与腹部有关的」。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'in the abdomen or by means of the abdomen'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在腹部；以腹部方式」。

entries.definition: An adjective, now rare, meaning 'having a large belly'.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，现已罕见，义为「大腹的；肥胖的」。

entries.definition: Cosmetic surgery that removes excess skin and fat from the abdomen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「腹壁整形术」，指切除腹部多余皮肤与脂肪的整形手术。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the front of the body below the chest.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「肚子」，是胸部以下身体前部的日常说法。

entries.definition: The organ that receives food, often used loosely for the whole belly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「胃」，也常宽松地指整个腹部。

entries.definition: A child-friendly or informal word for the belly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小肚肚」，是童语或非正式说法。

entries.definition: A large, often protruding belly, especially in an older man.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大肚腩」，尤指年长男性突出的肚子。

entries.definition: The intestines or the belly as a whole, used informally.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，非正式用法，义为「肠子」或整个腹部。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks work from the anatomical collocations and the family of adjectives; the abstract hooks picture the soft middle of the body.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点来自解剖搭配与形容词词族；抽象记忆点想象身体中段那个柔软的腔体。

normal.en: Lower abdomen and upper abdomen divide the belly into two clinical zones.
normal.cn: lower abdomen 与 upper abdomen 把肚子分成两个临床区域。

normal.en: Acute abdomen is the emergency label for sudden severe belly pain.
normal.cn: acute abdomen 是突发剧烈腹痛的急症标签。

normal.en: Abdominal is the adjective, as in abdominal muscles.
normal.cn: 形容词是 abdominal，如 abdominal muscles（腹部肌肉）。

normal.en: Abdominoplasty joins abdomen with the suffix for surgical reshaping.
normal.cn: abdominoplasty 把 abdomen 与表示外科整形的后缀组合起来。

normal.en: Insects and crabs also have an abdomen, because the word names the rear body section.
normal.cn: 昆虫和蟹也有 abdomen，因为这个词指后部体段。

abstract.en: Picture a soft pouch tied around the middle of the body, holding the stomach and intestines.
abstract.cn: 想象身体中段系着一个柔软的袋子，里面装着胃和肠。

abstract.en: Picture an insect drawn as three beads, with the last bead called the abdomen.
abstract.cn: 想象昆虫画成三颗珠子，最后一颗叫腹部。

abstract.en: Picture a doctor's two fingers pressing a patient's belly to find the sore spot.
abstract.cn: 想象医生的两根手指按在病人肚子上，寻找痛点。

examples.en: The pain began in the lower abdomen.
examples.cn: 疼痛从下腹部开始。

examples.en: A bee's abdomen is striped black and yellow.
examples.cn: 蜜蜂的腹部有黑黄条纹。

examples.en: The scan revealed a small mass in his abdomen.
examples.cn: 扫描发现他腹腔里有一个小结节。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布多门」——肚子像一扇门，里面藏着肠胃，门外只看见柔软的腹部。

root: 拉丁语 abdomen（肚子），来源不确定；一种推测与 abdere（藏起来）有关，因为腹部把内脏藏在其后

sensesIntro.en: The senses start with the human belly and its inner cavity, then spread to insects, crustaceans, and spiders, and finally to everyday and clinical uses.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从人的腹部与腹腔开始，扩展到昆虫、甲壳类与蜘蛛，最后落到日常与临床用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the soft middle chamber that holds the gut
core.cn: 核心意象：装着肠子的柔软中段腔体

branches.en: The human and vertebrate belly, seen from outside or as an inner cavity.
branches.cn: 人与脊椎动物的腹部，可从外部看，也可指内部腔体。

branches.en: The rear body section of arthropods, named by analogy with the gut-holding belly.
branches.cn: 节肢动物的后部体段，因同样容纳肠道而与人的腹部类比得名。

branches.en: The rounded everyday belly, often mentioned with a smile.
branches.cn: 日常中圆鼓的肚子，常带笑谈语气。

branches.en: The lower trunk as a comparative-anatomy region.
branches.cn: 作为比较解剖学区域的躯干下部。

branches.en: The clinical label for a sudden abdominal emergency.
branches.cn: 用于突发腹部急症的临床标签。

intro.en: The useful pieces are the Latin stem abdomin- and the adjective and adverb endings that build the medical family.
intro.cn: 有用的构件是拉丁词干 abdomin-，以及构成医学词族的形容词与副词后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin adjective abdominalis is the direct source of the English adjective, so the Latin entries record the same stem in its original endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形容词 abdominalis 是英语形容词的直接来源，因此拉丁条目记录的是同一词干在拉丁语中的词尾形式。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「腹部的」
名词，义为「腹壁整形术」

definition_zh: 腹部的；与腹有关的
definition_en: relating to the abdomen, the part of the body between the chest and the legs
core_image: 躯干中段的一圈，被一条腰带圈出的区域
scene: 训练课上，教练拍着自己的腰腹让大家照做。She was told to keep her abdominal muscles tight during the exercise.
sceneCN: 这里 abdominal 是「腹部的」（第 1 个义项：与腹有关的）；句意为她被要求在做动作时收紧腹部肌肉。

derivatives.zh: 同根名词，义为「腹部」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「在腹部方面」

senses.title: Of the belly region
senses.definition: belonging to or located in the part of the trunk between the chest and the pelvis
senses.definitionCN: 属于或位于躯干上胸下骨盆之间的那一部分
senses.example: An abdominal strain kept the player out of the match.
senses.exampleCN: 腹部拉伤让这名球员错过了比赛。
senses.why: The adjective is built directly on the Latin noun for the belly; it points at that one region of the trunk.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词直接建在拉丁语「腹部」名词之上；它指向躯干的那一个区域。

senses.title: Of structures on the underside
senses.titleCN: 位于腹侧或下方的（如鱼鳍）
senses.definition: of fins or other structures, positioned on the underside or belly side of an animal
senses.definitionCN: 指鱼鳍等结构位于动物的下腹一侧
senses.example: The characin has abdominal fins set far back on its body.
senses.exampleCN: 这种脂鲤的腹鳍长在身体很靠后的位置。
senses.why: In zoology the same region word labels whatever grows on the belly side, fins included.
senses.whyCN: 在动物学中，同一个部位词也用来标记长在腹侧的东西，鱼鳍也不例外。

intro.en: Abdominal is simply Latin abdomen plus the adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: abdominal 就是拉丁语 abdomen 加形容词后缀 -al。

items.en: Abdomen named the belly; its earlier origin is uncertain, possibly from abdere, to hide.
items.cn: 拉丁语 abdomen 指腹部；更早的来源不确定，一般认为可能与 abdere「藏」有关。

items.en: Abdominalis was formed in learned writing for things of the belly.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 abdominalis 在学术写作中构成，指与腹有关之物。

items.en: The adjective came into learned English through French medical texts.
items.cn: 该形容词经法语医学文献进入学术英语。

items.en: Abdominal settled in anatomy and medicine.
items.cn: 十七世纪起 abdominal 固定用于解剖学与医学。

items.en: It now appears in medicine, fitness, and zoology.
items.cn: 如今该词见于医学、健身与动物学。

note.en: The family is small: the noun abdomen and its Latin cousins.
note.cn: 这个词族很小：名词 abdomen 及其拉丁语近亲。

entries.definition: the noun for the belly
entries.definitionCN: 腹部名词，是 abdominal 的词基

entries.definition: detestable; only the opening letters match
entries.definitionCN: 可憎的；开头字母与 abdominal 相近，词源完全不同

entries.definition: the everyday word for the same region
entries.definitionCN: 同一部位的白话说法；belly 作形容词时用 belly-deep 等

entries.definition: of the underside of the body
entries.definitionCN: 腹面的；解剖学近义词

entries.definition: of the stomach specifically
entries.definitionCN: 胃部的；范围比腹部小

normalIntro.en: Five anchors tie abdominal to the waistline.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手把 abdominal 与腰腹绑在一起。

normal.en: abdomen + al: the belly turned into an adjective.
normal.cn: abdomen ＋ al：把「腹」变成形容词。

normal.en: abdominal muscles are the abs people train.
normal.cn: abdominal muscles 就是人们练的 abs。

normal.en: Compare ventral, the Latin biology twin.
normal.cn: 对比 ventral，生物学里的拉丁孪生词。

normal.en: Watch out for abominable, a false neighbour.
normal.cn: 小心 abominable 这个假邻居。

normal.en: Doctors use it for pain, cavity, and surgery.
normal.cn: 医生用它说 pain、cavity、surgery。

abstract.en: Feel a belt tightening around the middle.
abstract.cn: 感到一条腰带在腰腹收紧。

abstract.en: See a dotted line drawn on the torso.
abstract.cn: 看见躯干上画出的一条虚线。

abstract.en: Picture scales along a fish's underside.
abstract.cn: 想象鱼腹侧面排列的鳞片。

examples.en: He complained of sharp abdominal pain all night.
examples.cn: 他整夜诉说剧烈的腹痛。

examples.en: Strong abdominal muscles protect the lower back.
examples.cn: 强健的腹肌能保护下背部。

examples.en: The surgeon closed the abdominal incision with care.
examples.cn: 外科医生小心缝合了腹部切口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿爸练肚」——阿爸天天练肚子的肌肉

root: 拉丁语 abdomen「腹部」＋ 形容词后缀 -al（源自拉丁 -alis）。abdomen 更早来源不确定，一般认为可能与 abdere「隐藏」相关，属存疑说法。学源形容词经中世纪拉丁语 abdominalis 与法语医学文本进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses map one region: the human belly, and whatever sits on an animal's underside.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项对应同一个区域：人的腹部，以及动物腹侧的构造。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the middle band of the trunk, ringed by a belt.
core.cn: 核心意象：躯干中段，被腰带圈出的那一圈。

branches.en: THE HUMAN BELLY: pain, muscles, surgery all live here.
branches.cn: 人的腹部：疼痛、肌肉、手术都在这里。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL UNDERSIDE: fins and parts on the belly side.
branches.cn: 动物腹侧：长在腹面的鳍等构造。

branches.en: ONE REGION: both senses point at the belly side.
branches.cn: 同一区域：两个义项都指向腹侧。

branches.en: LEARNED LANGUAGE: both are technical over everyday belly.
branches.cn: 书面语：两者都比白话 belly 更正式。

branches.en: ADJECTIVE JOB: the word never names the organ itself.
branches.cn: 形容词职能：这个词从不指称器官本身。

intro.en: A Latin noun plus one adjective ending; nothing hidden.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁名词加一个形容词词尾，别无他物。

latinIntro.en: Abdomen is attested in Latin; its deeper origin remains uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: abdomen 见于拉丁语记载；其更深层来源仍不确定。

items.example: It was the Latin form of -al.
It builds ventral, a synonym family.
It builds gastric words, narrower in range.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 gastric 一类范围更窄的词。

definition_zh: 诱拐；绑架；（解剖学）外展；（逻辑）溯因推理
definition_en: the act of taking someone away by force or deception, or the movement of a limb away from the body
core_image: 一只手把人和物从原来的位置带走
scene: 监控里，一名男子抱起街边的孩子就上了车。Police launched an investigation into the abduction of a young boy.
sceneCN: 这里 abduction 是「诱拐、绑架」（第 1 个义项：非法带走他人）；句意为警方对一名男孩被诱拐展开调查。

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀构成，义为「诱拐；绑架；使外展」
由动词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「诱拐者；绑架者；外展肌」
由动词加表示被动者的后缀构成，义为「被绑架者；被诱拐者」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「溯因的；诱拐的」

senses.title: Taking a child away
senses.definition: the illegal taking away of a child, often by deception or force
senses.definitionCN: 以欺骗或暴力非法带走儿童
senses.example: The abduction of the child was caught on camera.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子被诱拐的过程被摄像头拍了下来。
senses.why: Latin abducere meant 'to lead away'; the noun abductio named the act of carrying someone off, and the criminal sense grew from that plain image.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abducere 意为「带走」；名词 abductio 指把人带离的行为，犯罪义项正是从这个朴素意象发展出来的。

senses.title: Kidnapping an adult
senses.definition: the act of seizing and carrying off an adult against their will
senses.definitionCN: 违背成人意愿将其抓住并带走
senses.example: The gang was convicted of the abduction of a businessman.
senses.exampleCN: 该团伙因绑架一名商人而被定罪。
senses.why: The same leading-away action applies to adults; the word stresses the carrying off rather than the ransom.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「带离」动作也适用于成人；这个词强调的是带走本身，而非赎金。

senses.title: Anatomical abduction
senses.definition: the movement of a limb or body part away from the midline of the body
senses.definitionCN: 肢体或身体部位离开身体中线的动作
senses.example: The therapist tested shoulder abduction through its full range.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗师完整测试了肩关节外展的活动范围。
senses.why: Anatomists reused the Latin verb for leading away: the limb is led away from the body's centre line.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学家沿用了这个表示「带走」的拉丁动词：肢体被带离身体中线。

senses.title: Abductive reasoning
senses.definition: a form of reasoning that infers the most likely explanation for an observation
senses.definitionCN: 为某个观察推断最可能解释的推理形式
senses.example: Detectives rely on abduction when they form a hypothesis from clues.
senses.exampleCN: 侦探根据线索提出假设时，依靠的正是溯因推理。
senses.why: Logic borrowed the term for 'leading away' because the mind is led away from the observed fact to a possible cause behind it.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学借用了「带走」这个词，因为思维被从观察到的事实带向其背后可能的原因。

senses.title: Unlawful taking in law
senses.definition: the legal charge for taking a person away unlawfully, especially a minor
senses.definitionCN: 法律上非法带走他人、尤指未成年人的罪名
senses.example: The court treated the case as abduction rather than a custody dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 法院把此案按诱拐处理，而非监护权纠纷。
senses.why: The law adopts the plain 'leading away' image and fixes it to a charge, so the act itself names the offence.
senses.whyCN: 法律采用「带走」这个朴素意象并把它固定为一项罪名，于是行为本身就成了罪名的名称。

senses.title: Carrying off young animals
senses.definition: the taking away of young animals from their group or parent
senses.definitionCN: 把幼崽从其群体或亲代身边带走
senses.example: Researchers recorded the abduction of a cub by a rival male.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员记录了一头幼崽被敌对雄性带走的情况。
senses.why: Field biology applies the human term to animals when one animal carries off another's young.
senses.whyCN: 野外生物学把人的术语用于动物，指一只动物带走另一只的幼崽。

senses.title: Muscle action of abducting
senses.definition: the action of a muscle that pulls a limb away from the midline
senses.definitionCN: 肌肉把肢体拉离中线的动作
senses.example: The abductor muscle performs abduction of the little finger.
senses.exampleCN: 外展肌完成小指的外展动作。
senses.why: The movement sense is narrowed to the muscle that produces it, so the noun can name the action of a specific muscle.
senses.whyCN: 动作义被收窄到产生它的肌肉上，因此这个名词也能指某块肌肉的具体动作。

senses.title: Alien abduction
senses.definition: a claimed case in which aliens take a person away, usually temporarily
senses.definitionCN: 声称外星人把人带走、通常短暂带离的说法
senses.example: The witness described an alleged alien abduction.
senses.exampleCN: 证人描述了一次据称的外星人绑架。
senses.why: Popular culture stretches the criminal image into science fiction, where the kidnappers come from the sky.
senses.whyCN: 流行文化把犯罪意象延伸到科幻领域，绑架者来自天上。

intro.en: Abduction goes back to a Latin verb meaning 'to lead away', built from a prefix of separation and the verb for leading.
intro.cn: abduction 可追溯到意为「带走」的拉丁语动词，由表示分离的前缀与表示「引导」的动词构成。

items.en: The root *deuk- is reconstructed with the sense 'to lead'; it also lies behind duke and duct.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *deuk- 被重构为「引导」之义；duke 与 duct 也源自它。

items.en: ducere meant 'to lead, draw'; it produced a large family including ductus and dux.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引导、拉」，衍生出 ductus、dux 等一大批词。

items.en: ab- 'away' plus ducere formed abducere, 'to lead away, carry off'.
items.cn: ab-（离开）与 ducere 构成 abducere，意为「带走、领走」。

items.en: The noun abductio named the act of leading away, including in anatomical writing.
items.cn: 名词 abductio 指带走的行为，解剖学文献中也有此用法。

items.en: English adopted abduction for the criminal sense and for the anatomical movement.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪吸收该词，用于犯罪义项与解剖学动作。

items.en: Logic added the sense of inference to the best explanation, and popular culture added alien abduction.
items.cn: 逻辑学补充了「最佳解释推断」之义，流行文化又补充了「外星人绑架」之义。

note.en: The first group gathers the verb, the person who acts, the person acted upon, and the adjective; the second gathers words for taking a person away.
note.cn: 第一组收动词、施动者、被施动者与形容词；第二组收表示把人带走的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to take someone away or to move a limb outward.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「诱拐、绑架」或「使肢体外展」。

entries.definition: A person who carries someone off, or a muscle that moves a limb away.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「诱拐者」或「外展肌」。

entries.definition: The person who has been taken away.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「被绑架者、被诱拐者」。

entries.definition: An adjective describing reasoning that infers a likely explanation.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「溯因的」，描述推断可能解释的推理。

entries.definition: The crime of seizing a person and holding them, often for ransom.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「绑架」，指抓走并扣押他人、常为索要赎金的罪行。

entries.definition: A quick, sudden taking away, often of a bag or a child.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「抢夺、迅速抓走」，常指抢包或抱走孩子。

entries.definition: The act of taking hold of someone or something by force.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「夺取、扣押」，指以武力抓住人或物。

entries.definition: The taking control of a vehicle or aircraft by force.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「劫持」，指以武力控制交通工具。

entries.definition: The act of catching and holding a person or animal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「捕获、俘获」，指抓住并扣留人或动物。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the Latin pieces, the anatomical pairing, and the criminal collocations; the abstract hooks picture the carrying away.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用拉丁构件、解剖学配对与犯罪搭配；抽象记忆点想象「带走」的动作。

normal.en: ab- means away and ducere means to lead, so abduction is literally a leading away.
normal.cn: ab- 表示离开，ducere 表示引导，因此 abduction 字面就是「带走」。

normal.en: Abduction and adduction are a pair: away from the midline and toward it.
normal.cn: abduction 与 adduction 是一对：一个离开中线，一个靠向中线。

normal.en: Child abduction and attempted abduction are common news collocations.
normal.cn: child abduction 与 attempted abduction 是常见新闻搭配。

normal.en: The abductor takes the abductee; the two endings keep the roles apart.
normal.cn: abductor 带走 abductee；两个后缀把施动者与受动者区分开。

normal.en: Abductive reasoning is the logic sense, inferring the best explanation.
normal.cn: abductive reasoning 是逻辑义，指推断最佳解释。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing on a small figure and pulling it out of the frame.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手抓住一个小小的人影，把它拉出画面。

abstract.en: Picture an arm lifting sideways, away from the centre line of the body.
abstract.cn: 想象一条手臂向侧面抬起，离开身体中线。

abstract.en: Picture a detective staring at footprints and following them back to a hidden door.
abstract.cn: 想象侦探盯着脚印，顺着它追到一扇隐藏的门。

examples.en: The police are investigating the abduction.
examples.cn: 警方正在调查这起绑架案。

examples.en: The doctor measured abduction of the shoulder.
examples.cn: 医生测量了肩关节的外展幅度。

examples.en: The theory rests on abduction from the observed data.
examples.cn: 该理论依靠从观察数据出发的溯因推理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱不打开」——有人把孩子抱起就走，爱他的人却打不开那扇车门。

root: 拉丁语 ab-（离开）+ ducere（引导），构成 abducere（带走）；核心义是「把人或肢体从原处带离」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from criminal taking, through anatomical movement, to logical inference and popular culture.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从犯罪的带走，经过解剖学动作，走到逻辑推断与流行文化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand leading someone away from where they belong
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把某人从其应在之处带走

branches.en: Criminal removal: a child or adult is taken against the law.
branches.cn: 犯罪的带离：儿童或成人被非法带走。

branches.en: Anatomical removal: a limb or muscle moves away from the midline.
branches.cn: 解剖学的带离：肢体或肌肉离开中线。

branches.en: Mental removal: the mind is led from a fact to a hidden cause.
branches.cn: 思维的带离：思维从事实被引向隐藏的原因。

branches.en: Animal removal: a cub is carried off from its group.
branches.cn: 动物的带离：幼崽被从群体中带走。

branches.en: Fictional removal: aliens carry a person away.
branches.cn: 虚构的带离：外星人把人带走。

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin prefix ab-, the verb stem duc-, and the noun ending -tion, with agent and patient endings in the family.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁前缀 ab-、动词词干 duc- 与名词后缀 -tion 构成，词族中还有施动者与受动者后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere is the shared source of a very large family, so the Latin entries show the verb and its noun rather than a single borrowed form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ducere 是一个庞大词族的共同来源，因此拉丁条目给出动词及其名词，而不是单一借词。

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「诱拐；绑架；使外展」
名词，义为「诱拐者；外展肌」
名词，义为「被绑架者」

definition_zh: 在床上（旧式用语）
definition_en: in bed; lying in bed (an old-fashioned or literary word)
core_image: 被褥里的人影，老式卧室烛光下的静态
scene: 窗纸透出微光，屋里静得只闻呼吸。The child was still abed long after the sun had risen.
sceneCN: 这里 abed 是「在床上」（第 1 个义项：卧于床上）；句意为太阳升起来很久，孩子还赖在床上。

pos.zh: 在床上；卧床（旧式、文学用法）

derivatives.zh: 词基名词，义为「床」
合成形容词，义为「卧床不起的」
同根旧式副词，义为「朝床的方向」

senses.title: In bed
senses.definition: lying in bed, or staying in bed
senses.definitionCN: 躺在床上，或待在床上
senses.example: The whole household was abed when the fire bell rang.
senses.exampleCN: 火警钟响起时，全家人都还在床上。
senses.why: The old English prefix a- means on or in; abed simply says on bed.
senses.whyCN: 古英语前缀 a- 意为「在……之上／之中」；abed 就是「在床上」的简单说法。

senses.title: Confined to bed by illness
senses.definition: kept in bed because of sickness, in older and literary style
senses.definitionCN: 因生病而困守床榻，属旧式或文学用法
senses.example: The old man lay sick abed through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 老人整个冬天都卧病在床。
senses.why: The same on-bed picture, held for a long time, turns from rest into confinement.
senses.whyCN: 同一幅「在床上」的画面一旦延长，休息便变成了困守。

intro.en: Abed is old English grammar fossilised: the prefix a- (on, in) fastened to bed.
intro.cn: abed 是被凝固的古英语语法：前缀 a-（在……上）直接接到 bed 之前。

items.en: The prefix a-, from on, formed adverbs of place like abedde.
items.cn: 源自 on 的前缀 a- 构成方位副词，如古英语 abedde。

items.en: Abedde shortened to abed and stayed common in daily speech.
items.cn: 中古英语 abedde 简化为 abed，在日常用语中很常见。

items.en: Writers used abed freely in plays and chronicles.
items.cn: 作家们在戏剧与编年史中自由使用 abed。

items.en: Everyday speech replaced abed with in bed.
items.cn: 日常口语逐渐以 in bed 取代 abed。

items.en: Abed survives as an old-fashioned or literary word.
items.cn: 如今 abed 仅作旧式或文学用语存留。

note.en: Abed belongs to the small English family of a- adverbs.
note.cn: abed 属于英语 a- 副词的小词族。

entries.definition: on board a ship or plane, built with the same a-
entries.definitionCN: 在船／机上；与 abed 同用 a- 构词法

entries.definition: sleeping, another a- adverb from the same logic
entries.definitionCN: 睡着的；同一逻辑构成的 a- 副词

entries.definition: out of the country, again with a-
entries.definitionCN: 在国外；同样以 a- 构成

entries.definition: the modern everyday phrase
entries.definitionCN: 现代日常说法，已取代 abed

entries.definition: forced to stay in bed by illness
entries.definitionCN: 因病长期卧床的；形容词

entries.definition: long-term confinement to bed
entries.definitionCN: 长期卧床状态；比 abed 程度更重

normalIntro.en: Five anchors tie abed to its two visible parts.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手把 abed 与它两个可见部件绑在一起。

normal.en: a- + bed = on bed.
normal.cn: a- ＋ bed ＝ 在床上。

normal.en: Same recipe as aboard, asleep, abroad.
normal.cn: 构词法与 aboard、asleep、abroad 相同。

normal.en: Abed sounds old-fashioned; in bed sounds normal.
normal.cn: abed 听上去老派；in bed 才是常话。

normal.en: Use it in stories, not in text messages.
normal.cn: 写故事可用，发短信别用。

normal.en: One e in the middle keeps it short.
normal.cn: 中间只有一个 e，拼写极短。

abstract.en: See a candle burning beside closed curtains.
abstract.cn: 看见紧闭的窗帘边燃着一支蜡烛。

abstract.en: Hear morning sounds passing by a sleeper.
abstract.cn: 听晨间声响从睡者身边经过。

abstract.en: Feel the blanket held up like a lid.
abstract.cn: 感到被子像盖子一样压着。

examples.en: By ten o'clock nobody in the house was still abed.
examples.cn: 到十点钟，家里没有人还赖在床上。

examples.en: The fever kept her abed for a fortnight.
examples.cn: 高烧让她卧床两周。

examples.en: The innkeeper found the traveller abed at noon.
examples.cn: 旅店老板中午发现那位旅客还躺着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「鹅趴床」——鹅趴在床上不起来

root: 古英语前缀 a-（源自介词 on「在……之上」）＋ bed「床」→ 古英语 abedde → 中古英语 abed。属 a- 类方位副词，与 aboard、asleep、abroad 同一构词模式。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses share the single picture of being on the bed: rest, and sickness that holds you there.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项共用「在床上」一幅画面：休息，以及把人困在床上的病。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure under blankets while the day goes on.
core.cn: 核心意象：白日已至，被褥下仍有一个身影。

branches.en: THE PLAIN ON-BED SENSE: simply still in bed.
branches.cn: 单纯的「在床上」：只是仍未起身。

branches.en: THE SICK BED: illness stretches the same picture.
branches.cn: 病榻：疾病把同一幅画面拉长。

branches.en: ONE A- PATTERN: both are adverbs, never adjectives.
branches.cn: 同一种 a- 模式：都是副词，不作形容词。

branches.en: STYLE MARK: using abed marks a text as old or literary.
branches.cn: 文风标记：用 abed 即标注文本的旧式文学色彩。

branches.en: STATIC STATE: both describe staying, not going.
branches.cn: 静态：两者都写「停留」而非「行动」。

intro.en: The word is a two-part English compound: one prefix, one noun.
intro.cn: 这个词是两件式的英语合成词：一个前缀加一个名词。

latinIntro.en: The parts are Germanic throughout; Latin contributed nothing except through French bede borrowings unrelated to bed.
latinIntro.cn: 各部件全部是日耳曼语源；拉丁语没有贡献——法语中与 bed 无关的借词另当别论。

items.exampleCN: 它是有记载的早期形式。
