definition_zh: 偏离常规；反常；一时的失常；测量偏差；光学像差；光行差；生物畸变；离群值
definition_en: a departure from what is usual or expected, and in science a systematic deviation in an image, a measurement, or a living form
core_image: 一条笔直的白色轨迹，在某个点忽然向外拐出一道弧，留下一小段偏斜的线。
scene: 会议开到一半气氛紧张。The committee treated the violent outburst as a momentary aberration rather than a sign of character.
sceneCN: 这里 aberration 是「一时的行为失常」（第 2 个义项）；句意：委员会把那次暴怒发作看作一时失常，而非性格的征兆。场景：会议室、被打断的发言、有人低头把这个词记进纪要。

derivatives.zh: 偏离常规的；异常的
偏离；反常状态
偏差性的；偏离所致的
（光学）带像差的

senses.title: A departure from the usual course
senses.titleCN: 偏离常轨：从该走的线上滑开
senses.definition: a single departure from what is normal, expected, or standard, usually treated as an exception rather than a rule
senses.definitionCN: 一次偏离正常、预期或标准的情况，通常被当作例外而非常态
senses.example: Any aberration in the machine's rhythm was logged by the night technician.
senses.exampleCN: 机器节奏上任何一点偏离，都会被夜班技师记录下来。
senses.why: Latin aberrare is to wander off a path. The word keeps that picture: something has left the line it was supposed to follow.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aberrare 就是“从路上走开”。这个词保留了那幅画面：某样东西离开了它本该跟随的线。

senses.title: A lapse in behaviour or judgement
senses.titleCN: 一时失常：脑子短暂离开常轨
senses.definition: a temporary failure of judgement or behaviour that is out of character for the person
senses.definitionCN: 一个人一时判断或行为失控，与其平常性格不符
senses.example: In a moment of aberration he agreed to sign the false report.
senses.exampleCN: 在一时糊涂中，他同意签署那份虚假报告。
senses.why: The moral use grows from the spatial one: a mind that wanders off its usual path is, for that moment, aberrated.
senses.whyCN: 道德义从空间义长出来：心念一旦离开平常的轨道，那一刻它就是“偏了”。

senses.title: A repeatable error in measurement
senses.titleCN: 测量偏差：仪器每次都偏那么一点
senses.definition: a repeatable deviation of an instrument or a measurement from the true value
senses.definitionCN: 仪器或测量结果对真值产生的、可重复出现的偏差
senses.example: The survey was corrected for a slight aberration in the theodolite.
senses.exampleCN: 测量队对经纬仪的一处轻微偏差做了修正。
senses.why: In optics and metrology the word names an error that returns every time, not a random slip. It is the instrument's signature.
senses.whyCN: 在光学与计量学里，这个词指每次都重现的误差，而不是偶然的滑脱；它是仪器留下的签名。

senses.title: Distortion in a lens image
senses.titleCN: 光学像差：镜头把一点摊成一片
senses.definition: a defect in which a lens or mirror fails to bring light to a single sharp focus, so the image is blurred or coloured at the edges
senses.definitionCN: 透镜或反射镜不能把光汇聚到一个清晰焦点，使图像模糊或边缘带色的缺陷
senses.example: Stars near the edge of the photograph show coma, a common aberration.
senses.exampleCN: 照片边缘的恒星出现彗差，这是一种常见的像差。
senses.why: Here the deviation belongs to the optical system, not the observer: rays wander away from the ideal focus point.
senses.whyCN: 这里的偏离属于光学系统而非观测者：光线离开了理想的焦点。

senses.title: The apparent shift of starlight
senses.titleCN: 光行差：星星看起来挪了位置
senses.definition: the apparent displacement of a celestial object caused by the observer's motion combined with the finite speed of light
senses.definitionCN: 观测者运动与光速有限共同造成的天体视位置偏移
senses.example: Bradley discovered the aberration of light while searching for stellar parallax.
senses.exampleCN: 布拉德利在寻找恒星视差时发现了光行差。
senses.why: The star does not move; the observer's motion tilts the incoming ray. The same Latin word now covers a wandering of light itself.
senses.whyCN: 恒星并没有动，是观测者的运动把入射光线倾斜了。同一个拉丁词现在覆盖了光本身的“游走”。

senses.title: A deviation in a living form
senses.titleCN: 生物畸变：长歪了的结构
senses.definition: a structural or chromosomal deviation from the normal form of an organism
senses.definitionCN: 生物体在结构或染色体上偏离正常形态
senses.example: The laboratory screened the tissue for chromosomal aberrations.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室筛查了该组织的染色体畸变。
senses.why: Biology borrowed the optical term: a chromosome that departs from the standard pattern is read like a distorted image.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了光学词：偏离标准模式的染色体，被读成一张走形的图像。

senses.title: A short disturbance of mind
senses.titleCN: 精神失常：短暂地离开清醒
senses.definition: a brief period of mental disturbance in which reasoning or perception departs from normal
senses.definitionCN: 一段短暂的精神紊乱，推理或感知偏离正常
senses.example: The old records describe bouts of aberration in which he spoke to people who were not there.
senses.exampleCN: 旧档案记载了他几次精神失常，对着并不存在的人说话。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century psychiatry used aberration for a mind off its track, keeping the root image of wandering.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪精神病学用 aberration 指偏离轨道的心智，保留了“游走”的词根意象。

senses.title: A point that breaks a trend
senses.definition: an observation that departs so far from the pattern of the data that it has to be treated separately
senses.definitionCN: 偏离数据整体模式太远、需要单独处理的观测值
senses.example: The analyst set the December spike aside as an aberration.
senses.exampleCN: 分析员把十二月那个尖峰当作离群点单独搁置。
senses.why: Statistics applies the same test as astronomy: one point has left the expected curve and must be explained.
senses.whyCN: 统计学用的是和天文一样的判断：有一个点离开了预期的曲线，必须解释它为什么离开。

intro.en: Aberration is built from two Latin pieces, ab- 'away' and errare 'to wander'. It reached English through astronomy and optics before it was ever used of people.
intro.cn: aberration 由两个拉丁成分构成：ab-“离开”与 errare“游走”。它先经天文学与光学进入英语，很久以后才用来形容人。

items.en: Errare meant to wander, stray, or roam, and is also the source of English error. A wanderer is not lost yet, only off the road.
items.cn: errare 意为游走、迷路、漫游，也是英语 error 的来源。游走的人尚未“失去”，只是离开了路。

items.en: The prefix ab- marks motion away from a point. Joined to a verb of motion it produces the idea of going off in the wrong direction.
items.cn: 前缀 ab- 表示“离开某点”的运动。与移动动词结合，就产生“朝错误方向走开”的意思。

items.en: To wander away from the proper path, hence to go astray or deviate. The word is spatial before it is moral.
items.cn: 偏离正道走开，因而“走入歧途、偏离”。这个词先有空间义，后有道德义。

items.en: A wandering off, a deviation. In classical Latin it could also mean a diversion or relief, an aside that turns the mind away; that cheerful sense did not survive into English.
items.cn: 偏离、走开。古典拉丁语中它还可指“消遣、散心”，即把心思引开的插曲；这个轻松义没有进入英语。

items.en: English borrowed the word for technical deviations: the apparent motion of light and the defects of lenses and mirrors.
items.cn: 英语 16 世纪借入该词，用于技术性的偏离：光的视运动，以及透镜与反射镜的缺陷。

items.en: The sense widened in the 18c-19c to behaviour, mental states, biology, and finally statistics, while the optical senses remained technical.
items.cn: 18 至 19 世纪，词义扩展到行为、精神状态、生物学，最后是统计学；光学的义项则一直保持技术性。

note.en: The first group is built from aberration itself; the second compares words for things that break a pattern, each with a different centre.
note.cn: 第一组由 aberration 自身派生；第二组比较同样表示“打破模式”的词，但各自的重心不同。

entries.definition: departing from the normal type. It describes the thing that has strayed, not the straying itself.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离正常类型的。它描述“已经走偏的东西”，而不是“走偏这件事”。

entries.definition: the quality or state of being aberrant. It is the abstract condition, not a single instance.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离常规的性质或状态；是抽象状态，而非某一次具体偏离。

entries.definition: relating to or caused by an aberration. It often modifies errors and effects.
entries.definitionCN: 与偏差有关的、由偏差引起的，常修饰误差与效应。

entries.definition: in optics, describing a lens or image that carries aberration. The word barely exists outside technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 光学中形容透镜或图像带有像差；几乎只出现在技术文献里。

entries.definition: a difference from an agreed standard or course. It is the neutral, measurable partner of aberration.
entries.definitionCN: 与约定标准或路线之间的差异；是 aberration 中性、可测量的伙伴。

entries.definition: something that does not fit a rule and cannot yet be explained. It stresses puzzlement rather than error.
entries.definitionCN: 不合规则且暂时无法解释的事物；强调困惑，而非错误。

entries.definition: the act of leaving an established way of doing something. It keeps the physical image of walking away.
entries.definitionCN: 离开既定做法；保留“走开”这一身体意象。

entries.definition: a person or thing that is simply strange. It carries no scientific measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅显得古怪的人或物，不带科学测量的意味。

entries.definition: a change in shape or meaning that twists the original. In optics it is one specific kind of aberration.
entries.definitionCN: 使原形或原意扭曲的变化；在光学中它只是像差的一种。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: ab- 'away' plus errare 'to wander'. The same errare gives English error; the same word family gives aberrant and aberrance.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：ab-“离开”加 errare“游走”。同一个 errare 也给出英语 error；同一词族还有 aberrant、aberrance。

normal.en: Ab- is away, err is wander: aberration is a wander away from the line.
normal.cn: ab- 是离开，err 是游走：aberration 就是离开那条线去游荡。

normal.en: Error and aberration are cousins: both come from Latin errare, to wander.
normal.cn: error 与 aberration 是表亲：都来自拉丁语 errare“游走”。

normal.en: In a lens, the rays wander off the focus and the star grows a halo.
normal.cn: 在镜头里，光线游离开焦点，星星就长出一圈光晕。

normal.en: A mental aberration is the mind taking a short walk off its usual road.
normal.cn: 精神失常，就是心智离开常走的路去散了一小会儿步。

normal.en: In statistics an aberration is the one dot that refuses to sit on the curve.
normal.cn: 统计里的 aberration，就是那个不肯坐在曲线上的点。

abstract.en: Every system defines a line; aberration is the price of having a line at all.
abstract.cn: 每个系统都定义了一条线；偏差，就是拥有这条线所付的代价。

abstract.en: An aberration is only visible against an expectation.
abstract.cn: 偏差，只有在期待存在时才看得见。

abstract.en: Light, minds, and data all wander in the same grammar.
abstract.cn: 光、心智与数据，用的是同一套“游走”的语法。

examples.en: The comet's position showed a tiny aberration that the old charts had missed.
examples.cn: 彗星的位置显示出旧星图漏掉的一处微小偏差。

examples.en: The coach called the team's poor first half an aberration, not a collapse.
examples.cn: 教练把球队上半场的糟糕表现称为一时失常，而不是崩盘。

examples.en: A chromatic aberration left purple fringes along the edge of the moon.
examples.cn: 色差在月亮边缘留下一圈紫色镶边。

dict_mnemonic.text: “啊，别惹人”——一偏离常轨，就“啊，别惹人注意”：aberration 偏离、反常

root: 源自拉丁语 aberrare（ab-“离开”+ errare“游走”），本义“游荡开去、偏离正道”，经 aberratio 进入英语；核心是“离开该走的那条线”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of aberration, all one movement: something leaves the line it should have followed. First in space, then in behaviour, instruments, light, living forms, minds, and finally data.
sensesIntro.cn: aberration 的八个义项都围绕同一个动作：某样东西离开了它本该跟随的线。先是在空间里，然后是行为、仪器、光、生物形态、心智，最后是数据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight track with one short arc bending away from it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条笔直的轨道，旁边岔出一小段弯出去的弧。

chain: A DEPARTURE FROM THE EXPECTED LINE
ANY FORM THAT LEAVES ITS PATTERN

branches.en: DEVIATION FROM A LINE: a general exception and a statistical outlier are both points off the fitted curve.
branches.cn: 偏离那条线：一般性的例外与统计离群点，都是落在拟合曲线之外的点。

branches.en: A MIND OFF ITS TRACK: a single lapse and a period of mental disturbance apply the same metaphor to judgement.
branches.cn: 离开轨道的心智：一时糊涂与一段精神紊乱，都是把同一比喻用在判断力上。

branches.en: INSTRUMENT ERROR: the deviation is built into the tool and repeats itself.
branches.cn: 仪器误差：偏差被造进工具里，并且会重复出现。

branches.en: LIGHT THAT MISSES THE FOCUS: a lens defect and the apparent shift of starlight both bend rays away from the ideal point.
branches.cn: 错过焦点的光：镜头缺陷与星光视偏移，都把光线弯离理想的那个点。

branches.en: FORM OFF ITS PATTERN: a chromosome or organ that departs from the standard shape.
branches.cn: 离开模式的形态：偏离标准形状的染色体或器官。

intro.en: Aberration carries the Latin prefix ab- and the suffix -ion. English builds the rest of the family with -ant, -ance, -al, and -ed.
intro.cn: aberration 带着拉丁前缀 ab- 与后缀 -ion；英语用 -ant、-ance、-al、-ed 造出其余词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain is errare 'to wander', ab- 'away', aberrare 'to go astray', and the noun aberratio. All four are real Latin forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语链条是 errare“游走”、ab-“离开”、aberrare“走入歧途”，以及名词 aberratio。四个都是真实的拉丁形式。

items.meaningCN: 偏离正常类型的（-ant 构成形容词）
items.example: The aberrant reading was checked against a second instrument.
items.exampleCN: 那个异常读数被拿去用第二台仪器核对。

items.meaningCN: 偏离常规的状态（-ance 构成状态名词）
items.example: The botanist noted the aberrance of the leaf shape.
items.exampleCN: 植物学家记下了叶形的异常。

items.meaning: an instance or condition of deviation
items.meaningCN: 偏离的实例或状况（-ancy 为 -ance 的变体）
items.example: The committee reported several aberrancies in the accounts.
items.exampleCN: 委员会报告了账目中的若干异常。

items.meaning: relating to or caused by an aberration
items.meaningCN: 与偏差有关的、由偏差引起的（-al 构成关系形容词）
items.example: The signal was dismissed as an aberrational blip.
items.exampleCN: 那个信号被当作偏差性的短暂脉冲排除了。

items.meaningCN: 带有光学像差的（-ate + -ed 构成技术分词）
items.example: An aberrated wavefront blurs the image.
items.exampleCN: 带像差的波前会使图像模糊。

items.meaning: the apparent shift of a star caused by the observer's motion
items.meaningCN: 观测者运动造成的恒星视位置偏移（固定术语）
items.example: The aberration of light was measured to within a second of arc.
items.exampleCN: 光行差被测量到角秒以内的精度。

items.meaning: a change in chromosome structure or number
items.meaningCN: 染色体结构或数目的改变（技术复合词）
items.example: The screening looked for chromosomal aberration in the sample.
items.exampleCN: 筛查在样本中寻找染色体畸变。

items.meaning: blurring because a spherical lens focuses rays at different points
items.meaningCN: 球面透镜把光线聚在不同焦点而造成的模糊（光学复合词）
items.example: Stopping down the lens reduced the spherical aberration.
items.exampleCN: 缩小光圈减轻了球面像差。

items.structure: in + a moment of + aberration (fixed phrase)
items.meaning: during a brief lapse of judgement
items.meaningCN: 在一时判断失常之际（固定短语）
items.example: In a moment of aberration she told him the truth.
items.exampleCN: 在一时冲动中，她把真相告诉了他。

items.meaning: designed so that no aberration occurs
items.meaningCN: 无像差的；设计上不产生偏差的（复合形容词）
items.example: The new telescope uses an aberration-free design.
items.exampleCN: 新望远镜采用了无像差设计。

latinEntries.meaning: to wander away from the right path
latinEntries.meaningCN: 离开正道走开；走入歧途

definition_zh: 教唆；煽动；帮助（尤指做坏事）
definition_en: to encourage or help someone to do something wrong, especially a crime
core_image: 站在作案者身后递工具、打手势的那个人
scene: 法庭上，检察官指着第二被告席。He was charged with aiding and abetting the robbery.
sceneCN: 这里 abet 是「教唆、协助犯罪」（第 2 个义项：法律用语中的协助）；句意为他被控抢劫罪的协助与教唆。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -er 构成，义为「教唆者；唆使者」
abetter 的法律变体，义为「教唆犯；协助犯」
由动词加 -ment 构成，义为「教唆行为」

senses.title: To encourage wrongdoing
senses.definition: to urge or encourage someone to do something bad or dishonest
senses.definitionCN: 怂恿或鼓励某人做坏事或不诚实之事
senses.example: His classmates abetted his plan to skip school.
senses.exampleCN: 同学们怂恿他逃学的计划。
senses.why: An old French phrase meant to bite a dog on to fight; urging another on is the heart of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古法语短语原指纵狗撕咬；「促使他人向前」正是这个词的核心。

senses.title: To help commit a crime
senses.definition: to help or support someone in committing a criminal act
senses.definitionCN: 帮助或支持他人实施犯罪行为
senses.example: The driver was convicted of aiding and abetting the escape.
senses.exampleCN: 司机被判协助教唆逃跑罪。
senses.why: Law fixed the loose sense into a charge: the helper behind the act shares the guilt.
senses.whyCN: 法律把松散的含义固定为一项罪名：行动背后的协助者同担罪责。

senses.title: To support or back a venture
senses.definition: to support or promote an undertaking, in older or ironical use
senses.definitionCN: 支持或推动某项事业，属旧式或反讽用法
senses.example: The committee's silence abetted the rumour.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会的沉默助长了谣言。
senses.why: Urging-on does not always serve crime; pointed at gossip or plans, it only means pushing them along.
senses.whyCN: 「催促向前」并非只为罪恶服务；指向谣言或计划时，它只表示推波助澜。

intro.en: Abet comes from an Old French phrase about setting dogs on to fight, later widened to inciting anyone.
intro.cn: abet 来自一个关于纵狗相斗的古法语短语，后扩大为「煽动任何人」。

items.en: Aider bercer or abeter meant to bait, to set dogs on.
items.cn: 古法语 abeter 意为纵狗、诱使撕咬。

items.en: The French verb is thought to hold a Germanic element for biting, related to bait.
items.cn: 一般认为该法语动词含一个日耳曼语「咬」的成分，与 bait 相关。

items.en: Abetten meant to incite, especially hounds or fighters.
items.cn: 中古英语 abetten 意为煽动，尤指唆使猎犬或斗士。

items.en: Aid and abet became a fixed legal pair by the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪起，aid and abet 成为固定的法律搭配。

items.en: The crime senses now dominate; neutral uses survive as irony.
items.cn: 如今犯罪义占主导；中性用法仅存于反语。

note.en: Abet pairs with aid in law and rhymes with bet, which is no relative.
note.cn: abet 在法律上与 aid 搭配，与 bet 押韵但毫无亲缘。

entries.definition: a person who abets
entries.definitionCN: 教唆者；abet 的施动名词

entries.definition: the act of abetting
entries.definitionCN: 教唆行为；名词形式

entries.definition: to torment or lure, from the same biting root
entries.definitionCN: 逗弄、诱使；一般认为与 abet 同出「咬」词根

entries.definition: to stir up violent or unlawful action
entries.definitionCN: 煽动暴力或非法行动；语气更烈

entries.definition: to start something bad by urging
entries.definitionCN: 怂恿发起坏事；强调发起

entries.definition: to give support or hope
entries.definitionCN: 鼓励、支持；中性词，无犯罪色彩

normalIntro.en: Five anchors tie abet to the helper behind the crime.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手把 abet 与罪案背后的协助者绑在一起。

normal.en: aid and abet: the fixed legal pair.
normal.cn: aid and abet：固定的法律搭配。

normal.en: a- + bet picture: someone placing stakes on your bad bet.
normal.cn: 形象联想：有人给你的坏赌注下注。

normal.en: Double t in abetted and abetting.
normal.cn: 过去式与现在分词要双写 t。

normal.en: abetter or abettor: the person who abets.
normal.cn: abetter 或 abettor：教唆者。

normal.en: Encourage is neutral; abet smells of courtrooms.
normal.cn: encourage 是中性的；abet 带着法庭气息。

abstract.en: See a shadowed figure nodding behind the thief.
abstract.cn: 看见窃贼身后一个点头示意的人影。

abstract.en: Feel a hand pushing from the dark.
abstract.cn: 感到黑暗中有一只手在推。

abstract.en: Hear a whisper saying just do it.
abstract.cn: 听见一声「干吧」的低语。

examples.en: Nobody abetted him; the idea was entirely his own.
examples.cn: 没有人教唆他；主意完全是他自己的。

examples.en: She was accused of abetting the smugglers.
examples.cn: 她被指控协助走私者。

examples.en: Indifference can abet injustice as surely as wicked hands.
examples.cn: 冷漠与黑手一样会助长不公。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我帮你」——我不帮你谁帮你，一帮就帮上了贼船

root: 古法语 abeter「纵狗撕咬、诱使」，一般认为含日耳曼语词根「咬」（与 bait 同源），构成成分属重构说法。中古英语 abetten 指煽动，法律短语 aid and abet 自十五世纪沿用。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses push one gesture forward: urging on, abetting a crime, and ironic backing.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项推进同一个手势：煽动、协助犯罪、以及反讽的「支持」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand behind the doer, pushing him over the line.
core.cn: 核心意象：行事者身后有一只手，把他推过界线。

branches.en: THE URGE: words and nods that set another moving.
branches.cn: 怂恿：让对方动起来的言语与点头。

branches.en: THE CRIME PARTNER: the law makes the pusher a criminal too.
branches.cn: 罪案同伙：法律把推动者也定罪。

branches.en: THE QUIET PUSH: doing nothing on purpose also helps.
branches.cn: 无声的推动：刻意的沉默同样是帮助。

branches.en: ACTIVE ENCOURAGEMENT: both senses need visible urging.
branches.cn: 主动怂恿：这两个义项都需要明显的煽动。

branches.en: ONE PUSH: every sense is help from behind.
branches.cn: 同一次推：每个义项都是背后的助力。

intro.en: The word is a French phrase verb worn down to one syllable.
intro.cn: 这个词由法语短语动词磨损而成单音节词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root lies behind abet; its source is Germanic through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: abet 背后没有拉丁词根；其来源是经古法语传入的日耳曼语。

items.structure: Old French prefix from Latin ad-
items.example: It points the action at the victim.
It holds the Germanic bite root.
They double the t: abetted, abetting.

items.exampleCN: 它们构成 abetter 与 abettor。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -er 构成，义为「教唆者」
法律变体，义为「教唆犯」
由动词加 -ment 构成，义为「教唆行为」

definition_zh: 暂时无效；中止；搁置
definition_en: a state of temporary inactivity or suspension
core_image: 钟摆停在最边上的位置，等着下一次推动
scene: 新楼规划公示已挂半年，邻里都在等消息。The building plan has been in abeyance since the funding fell through.
sceneCN: 这里 abeyance 是「中止、搁置」（第 1 个义项：暂时停摆的状态）；句意为自资金落空后，建楼计划一直处于搁置状态。

pos.zh: 暂时无效；中止；搁置（状态）

derivatives.zh: 由名词加 -ant 构成，义为「中止的；暂时无效的」
法律短语名词，义为「暂缓条款」

senses.title: Temporary suspension of activity
senses.definition: a state in which something expected or ongoing is stopped for a while
senses.definitionCN: 预期进行之事被暂停一段时间的状态
senses.example: Negotiations were held in abeyance until the elections ended.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判被搁置，直到选举结束。
senses.why: Old French abeance meant a gazing or longing toward something; the matter stands looking at its goal without moving.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 abeance 意为「对某事张望渴求」；事情就那样望着目标而不动。

senses.title: Undetermined ownership or title
senses.definition: a legal state in which a right, title, or succession is not settled
senses.definitionCN: 权利、所有权或继承尚未确定的法律状态
senses.example: The barony fell into abeyance among several heirs.
senses.exampleCN: 男爵爵位在数位继承人之间处于悬置状态。
senses.why: When no one can hold the right, the law lets it stand open like a chair no one sits in.
senses.whyCN: 当无人能持有时，法律让它像一把无人落座的椅子般空着。

senses.title: A lapsed custom
senses.definition: a custom or practice that has gradually stopped being observed
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐停止被遵行的惯例
senses.example: The old ceremony fell into abeyance two generations ago.
senses.exampleCN: 那项古老仪式两代人以前便不再举行。
senses.why: What once moved regularly can slow until it stands still; the word names that standing still.
senses.whyCN: 曾经规律运行的事物会慢下来直至停摆；这个词命名的就是这种停摆。

intro.en: Abeyance descends from Old French abeance, a gazing or expectancy, built on a verb meaning to gape at.
intro.cn: abeyance 源自古法语 abeance「张望、期待」，其动词意为「对……张口凝视」。

items.en: A Frankish root for gaping is reconstructed behind the French verb, related to abash's source.
items.cn: 法语动词背后重构出一个法兰克语「张口」词根，与 abash 的来源相关。

items.en: Abeer meant to gape at or aspire; abeance was the state of longing attention.
items.cn: 古法语 abeer 意为凝望、渴求；abeance 指渴慕注视的状态。

items.en: Abeyance entered English law for ownership waiting to settle.
items.cn: 盎格鲁-法语 abeyance 进入英国法律，指待定的所有权。

items.en: The word widened to any temporary stop.
items.cn: 十六世纪起该词扩大为一切暂时中止。

items.en: In abeyance remains the standard phrase for suspension.
items.cn: in abeyance 至今仍是表示中止的标准短语。

note.en: Abeyance keeps company with other suspension words and shares an old root with abash.
note.cn: abeyance 与其他「中止」类词同群，并与 abash 共享一个古老的词根。

entries.definition: to embarrass, from the same gaping root
entries.definitionCN: 使窘迫；与 abeyance 同出「张口」词根

entries.definition: adjective meaning suspended
entries.definitionCN: 形容词形式，义为中止的

entries.definition: a temporary stopping
entries.definitionCN: 暂停；语域更通用

entries.definition: an official delay or halt
entries.definitionCN: 正式的延期或冻结；多为官方决定

entries.definition: an uncertain waiting state

normalIntro.en: Five anchors tie abeyance to the paused clock.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手把 abeyance 与停摆的钟绑在一起。

normal.en: in abeyance is the phrase to memorise.
normal.cn: 要背的短语是 in abeyance。

normal.en: Picture a pendulum stopped mid-swing.
normal.cn: 想象钟摆停在半摆的位置。

normal.en: Lawyers use it for unsettled titles.
normal.cn: 律师用它表示权属未定。

normal.en: fall into abeyance: a custom quietly dying.
normal.cn: fall into abeyance：惯例悄悄废止。

normal.en: It shares its gaping root with abash.
normal.cn: 它与 abash 共享「张口」词根。

abstract.en: Hear music stop between two bars.
abstract.cn: 听见乐声在两小节之间停住。

abstract.en: See a revolving door frozen halfway.
abstract.cn: 看见旋转门冻在半途。

abstract.en: Feel the pause where a decision should be.
abstract.cn: 感到本该有决定之处的停顿。

examples.en: The rule remained in abeyance until the board met again.
examples.cn: 在董事会再次开会之前，该规则一直搁置未行。

examples.en: Traffic fines were held in abeyance during the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水期间交通罚款暂停执行。

examples.en: The title fell into abeyance when the last baron died without a son.
examples.cn: 末代男爵无子而终，爵位遂陷入悬置。

root: 古法语 abeance「凝望渴求」＝ a-（拉丁 ex- 之转）＋ beance「张口」（日耳曼语源，与 abash 同词根，词根属重构形式）。经盎格鲁-法语进入英国法律，再扩大为一般「中止」义。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses hold one pose: standing still before a goal, whether law, plan, or custom.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项保持同一姿态：在目标前静止，无论是法律、计划还是惯例。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pendulum frozen at the edge of its swing.
core.cn: 核心意象：钟摆冻在摆动的边缘。

branches.en: THE PAUSED PLAN: activity stops but may resume.
branches.cn: 暂停的计划：活动停止但可恢复。

branches.en: THE OPEN SEAT: a right waits with no holder.
branches.cn: 空着的座位：权利等待持有者。

branches.en: THE SLEEPING CUSTOM: practice that quietly stopped.
branches.cn: 沉睡的惯例：悄悄停止的实践。

branches.en: TIME HOLDS STILL: both senses are pauses that stretch.
branches.cn: 时间静止：这两个义项都是延长的暂停。

branches.en: ONE STANDING STILL: every sense is motion withheld, not ended.
branches.cn: 同一种静止：每个义项都是被搁置而非终止的运动。

intro.en: A French prefix and a Germanic root meet in one noun ending.
intro.cn: 法语前缀与日耳曼词根在一个名词词尾中会合。

latinIntro.en: Only the prefix a- goes back to Latin ex-; the gaping root is Germanic and reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 只有前缀 a- 可回溯到拉丁语 ex-；「张口」词根属日耳曼语重构形式。

definition_zh: 遵守；持续存在；居住
definition_en: the act of obeying a rule, continuing in a state, or dwelling somewhere
core_image: 一个人稳稳站在规则划出的圈内不动
scene: 质检员把手册翻到最后一页，合上了。Compliance depends on the abidance of every workshop by the safety rules.
sceneCN: 这里 abidance 是「遵守」（第 1 个义项：依规行事）；句意为达标取决于每个车间对安全规则的遵守。

derivatives.zh: 词基动词，义为「遵守；忍受；持续；居住」
由现在分词转形容词，义为「持久的」
加否定前缀 non- 构成，义为「不遵守」

senses.title: Obedience to rules
senses.definition: the act of acting in accordance with a law, rule, or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 依照法律、规则或协议行事的行为
senses.example: The contract requires abidance by all local regulations.
senses.exampleCN: 合同要求遵守所有地方性法规。
senses.why: To abide originally meant to wait or stand firm; keeping a rule is standing inside its lines.
senses.whyCN: abide 本义为等候、坚持；守规则就是在规则划出的线内站立不动。

senses.title: Continuance in a state
senses.definition: the fact of continuing in a condition, place, or office
senses.definitionCN: 在某种状态、地点或职位上继续存在
senses.example: His abidance in the chairmanship surprised the younger members.
senses.exampleCN: 他继续担任主席让年轻成员感到意外。
senses.why: The waiting sense grows into lasting; to stay put through time is to abide and its noun abidance.
senses.whyCN: 「等候」之义延伸为「持久」；在时间中停在原处，就是 abide，其名词即 abidance。

senses.title: Dwelling
senses.definition: the act of living or staying in a place, an older use
senses.definitionCN: 在某地生活或停留，属较旧用法
senses.example: Their abidance in the mountain village lasted thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在山村一住就是三十年。
senses.why: Standing firm in a rule and standing firm in a place share one verb; residence is only the place-shaped version.
senses.whyCN: 坚守规则与坚守一地共用同一个动词；居住只是其「场所化」的版本。

intro.en: Abidance is the noun of abide, an Old English verb for waiting and enduring, plus the noun ending -ance.
intro.cn: abidance 是 abide 的名词形式；abide 是古英语表示等候、忍受的动词，加名词后缀 -ance 构成。

items.en: A root meaning to wait or persist is reconstructed for the Germanic family.
items.cn: 日耳曼语族重构出一个意为等候、持续的词根。

items.en: Abidan meant to wait for, to endure, to remain.
items.cn: 古英语 abidan 意为等候、忍受、留下。

items.en: Abiten widened to dwelling and tolerating.
items.cn: 中古英语 abiten 扩展出居住与容忍之义。

items.en: Abidance was formed with the French-style suffix -ance.
items.cn: 近代英语以法语式后缀 -ance 构成 abidance。

items.en: The noun is now rare; abide by the rules lives on as a phrase.
items.cn: 如今该名词少见；abide by the rules 作为短语沿用。

note.en: Abidance stands with the abide family, whose members are far more common.
note.cn: abidance 与 abide 词族并列，该词族成员远比它常用。

entries.definition: the verb meaning to stay, endure, or obey
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为停留、忍受、遵守

entries.definition: lasting, as in abiding memory

entries.definition: a dwelling, the place-noun of the family
entries.definitionCN: 住所；该词族的场所名词

entries.definitionCN: 遵守；现代语域中最常用

entries.definition: the keeping of laws or customs
entries.definitionCN: 遵行；稍显正式

entries.definitionCN: 符合；强调与标准一致

normalIntro.en: Five anchors tie abidance to the standing figure.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手把 abidance 与站立不动的人绑在一起。

normal.en: abide + ance: the noun of standing firm.
normal.cn: abide ＋ ance：「坚持站立」的名词。

normal.en: abide by the rules is the living phrase.
normal.cn: 活着的是短语 abide by the rules。

normal.en: abiding memory: a memory that stays.
normal.cn: abiding memory：留得住的记忆。

normal.en: abode is the family's house word.
normal.cn: abode 是这个词族的「住所」词。

normal.en: Abidance itself sounds bookish and rare.
normal.cn: abidance 本身听上去书面且少见。

abstract.en: See chalk lines drawn on a courtroom floor.
abstract.cn: 看见法庭地板上画出的粉笔线。

abstract.en: Feel one foot planted through a long wait.
abstract.cn: 感到长久的等待中一只脚稳稳踏住。

abstract.en: Watch a flagpole holding through the storm.
abstract.cn: 看旗杆在风暴中纹丝不动。

examples.en: Award of the licence is conditional on abidance by the zoning rules.
examples.cn: 执照的颁发以遵守分区规划规则为条件。

examples.en: The treaty praised the abidance of both states by the ceasefire.
examples.cn: 条约赞扬两国对停火协议的遵守。

examples.en: Their long abidance in the old mill house became local legend.
examples.cn: 他们对老磨坊宅的长久居住成了当地传说。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我白等死」——我宁可白等也不离开，坚守到底

root: 古英语 abidan「等候；忍受；留下」＝ a-（加强或方位前缀）＋ bidan「等候、期待」，出自原始日耳曼语重构词根「等候」。abidance 为近代英语以 -ance 后缀构成的名词化形式。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses keep one stance: standing within a rule, a state, or a place.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项保持同一种姿态：站在规则之内、状态之内、地点之内。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure standing inside a chalked circle, unmoved.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在粉笔圈内，纹丝不动。

branches.en: THE RULE LINE: obedience is standing inside the lines.
branches.cn: 规则之线：遵守就是站在线内。

branches.en: THE TIME LINE: continuance is standing through the years.
branches.cn: 时间之线：持续就是经年站立。

branches.en: THE PLACE LINE: dwelling is standing in one spot.
branches.cn: 地点之线：居住就是站在一处。

branches.en: FIRMNESS: both senses take the unyielding posture.
branches.cn: 坚定：这两个义项都取不肯退让的姿态。

branches.en: ONE STANCE: rule, time, and place are three frames of staying.
branches.cn: 同一姿态：规则、时间、地点是「停留」的三种框架。

intro.en: An Old English verb wears a French-style noun ending.
intro.cn: 一个古英语动词戴上法语式的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The verb root is Germanic; Latin enters only through the -ance suffix pattern.
latinIntro.cn: 动词词根属日耳曼语；拉丁语仅通过 -ance 后缀的模式进入。

definition_zh: 卑贱的；悲惨的；糟透的
definition_en: extremely low in condition, spirit, or quality; miserable
core_image: 被扔到门外的人，蜷在最低处的台阶上
scene: 失业又欠租，他站在粥棚队尾不敢抬头。After losing everything, he lived in abject poverty for years.
sceneCN: 这里 abject 是「悲惨的、赤贫的」（第 2 个义项：处境极度低下）；句意为失去一切之后，他多年生活在赤贫之中。

pos.zh: 卑贱的；卑微的（形容处境）
悲惨的；糟透的（形容状态或品质）

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「卑贱地；悲惨地」
由形容词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「卑贱；悲惨境况」

senses.title: Lacking self-respect
senses.definition: behaving in a way that shows no pride or dignity
senses.definitionCN: 表现出毫无骄傲或尊严的样子
senses.example: He made an abject apology for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 他为延误低声下气地道歉。
senses.why: The Latin root jacere means to throw; a person thrown down and out lies at the lowest point, without standing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 jacere 意为抛掷；被扔出去的人躺在最低处，站不起来。

senses.title: Extremely miserable in condition
senses.definition: in a state of extreme poverty, suffering, or misery
senses.definitionCN: 处于极度贫穷、痛苦或悲惨之中
senses.example: The refugees arrived in abject poverty and fear.
senses.exampleCN: 难民们带着赤贫与恐惧抵达。
senses.why: Being cast out strips everything; what is thrown away ends up in the worst condition.
senses.whyCN: 被抛出去意味着失去一切；被丢弃之物落得最坏的处境。

senses.title: Utterly bad in quality
senses.definition: of a quality or outcome, completely bad or without success
senses.definitionCN: 指品质或结果极差、毫无成功可言
senses.example: The campaign ended in abject failure.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动以彻底失败告终。
senses.why: The thrown-down image measures how low a result can sink; the worst outcome is the furthest down.
senses.whyCN: 「被抛落」的意象衡量结果能落到多低；最坏的结局就是坠得最深的那一个。

intro.en: Abject is Latin face to face: ab-, away, plus jacere, to throw; it describes what has been thrown out and down.
intro.cn: abject 是原样的拉丁语：ab-「离开」加 jacere「抛掷」；它描述被抛出去、摔到低处之物。

items.en: The root ye- meant to throw or hurl.
items.cn: 原始印欧词根 ye- 意为投掷。

items.en: Jacere meant to throw; abiectus was the participle, thrown away.
items.cn: 拉丁语 jacere 意为抛掷；abiectus 是其分词形式「被抛弃的」。

items.en: Abject passed through French as a learned adjective.
items.cn: abject 作为学术形容词经法语传递。

items.en: English adopted abject for the lowly and the miserable.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语借入 abject，指卑下者与悲惨者。

items.en: It now intensifies nouns like poverty, fear, and failure.
items.cn: 如今它作强化语，修饰 poverty、fear、failure 等名词。

note.en: Abject belongs to the jac- throw family, which includes project and reject.
note.cn: abject 属于 jac-「抛掷」词族，project、reject 都在其中。

entries.definitionCN: 名词形式，义为卑贱、悲惨境况

entries.definition: in a hopeless, servile way
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式，义为卑贱地

entries.definition: to throw back or refuse
entries.definitionCN: 拒绝、退回；同根 jacere 但前缀不同

entries.definition: very unhappy or of very poor quality
entries.definitionCN: 极不幸的；品质极差

entries.definition: behaving like a slave, overly eager to please
entries.definitionCN: 奴颜婢膝的；对应第 1 义项

entries.definition: without the basic means of life
entries.definitionCN: 一无所有的；对应赤贫义项

normalIntro.en: Five anchors tie abject to the thrown-down figure.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手把 abject 与被抛落的身影绑在一起。

normal.en: ab- away + ject throw: thrown out and down.
normal.cn: ab-（离开）＋ ject（抛掷）：被扔出去摔到低处。

normal.en: Same ject as in project, reject, inject.
normal.cn: ject 同见于 project、reject、inject。

normal.en: abject poverty is the classic pairing.
normal.cn: abject poverty 是经典搭配。

normal.en: abject apology: kneeling while saying sorry.
normal.cn: abject apology：跪着道歉。

normal.en: abject failure: as low as a result can go.
normal.cn: abject failure：跌到谷底的结局。

abstract.en: See a figure on the lowest step of a dark stair.
abstract.cn: 看见黑暗楼梯最低一级上的身影。

abstract.en: Feel mud at the bottom of a pit.
abstract.cn: 感到坑底烂泥的触感。

abstract.en: Hear the last coin drop from a torn pocket.
abstract.cn: 听见最后一枚硬币从破口袋坠落。

examples.en: They lived in abject poverty after the factory closed.
examples.cn: 工厂关闭后，他们生活在赤贫之中。

examples.en: His abject surrender shocked even his allies.
examples.cn: 他屈辱的投降连盟友都为之震惊。

examples.en: The team's abject performance cost the coach her job.
examples.cn: 球队糟透的表现让教练丢了工作。

root: 拉丁语 abiectus「被抛掉的」＝ ab-「离开」＋ jacere「抛掷」（原始印欧词根 ye-「投掷」）。经法语作为书面形容词进入英语，十五世纪起用。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses measure one fall: thrown-down pride, thrown-down fortune, thrown-down results.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项衡量同一次坠落：被抛下的尊严、被抛下的境遇、被抛下的结果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure cast out the door, lying on the lowest step.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人被扔出门外，躺在最低的台阶上。

branches.en: THE BENT BACK: dignity is the first thing thrown away.
branches.cn: 弯下的脊背：尊严是最先被抛弃的。

branches.en: THE EMPTY HANDS: fortune follows dignity to the bottom.
branches.cn: 空空的双手：境遇随尊严跌到谷底。

branches.en: THE DEAD END: outcomes sink to the same lowest place.
branches.cn: 死路：结果沉到同一个最低处。

branches.en: HUMAN MISERY: both senses describe persons in the pit.
branches.cn: 人的悲惨：这两个义项都写坑中之人。

branches.en: ONE FALL: every sense is a depth below the ordinary line.
branches.cn: 同一次坠落：每个义项都是平常线以下的深度。

intro.en: A Latin participle kept whole: prefix, root, and ending all visible.
intro.cn: 一个保存完好的拉丁分词：前缀、词根、词尾都清晰可见。

latinIntro.en: Latin jacere and abiectus are classical, recorded forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 jacere 与 abiectus 均为有记载的古典形式。

definition_zh: 发誓放弃；郑重宣告弃绝
definition_en: to swear formally that you give up a belief, claim, or way of acting
core_image: 一只手按在誓言书上，口中宣告与旧信仰断绝
scene: 宗教法庭的大厅里，笔与蜡烛都已备好。Under pressure, the scholar was made to abjure his former opinions.
sceneCN: 这里 abjure 是「发誓放弃」（第 1 个义项：郑重宣告弃绝信念）；句意为在压力之下，学者被迫宣誓放弃他原先的观点。

pos.zh: 发誓放弃；郑重弃绝（信念、主张）
公开宣布永久戒绝（行为、习惯）

collocations.zh: 宣誓放弃居留本国（历史用法）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「誓绝；弃国誓」
同根近形词，义为「郑重的恳求或告诫」

senses.title: To renounce under oath a belief or claim
senses.definition: to give up a belief, opinion, or right while swearing that the giving up is final
senses.definitionCN: 以誓言保证最终性的方式放弃信仰、观点或权利
senses.example: Galileo was made to abjure the doctrine he had defended.
senses.exampleCN: 伽利略被迫宣誓放弃他曾捍卫的学说。
senses.why: The root iurare means to swear; renouncing under oath turns a private change of mind into a public, binding act.
senses.whyCN: 词根 iurare 意为起誓；在誓言之下弃绝，使私下的改念成为公开而有约束力的行为。

senses.title: To swear off a course of action
senses.definition: to promise solemnly never to do a thing again
senses.definitionCN: 郑重承诺永不再做某事
senses.example: The defeated faction abjured the use of force.
senses.exampleCN: 失败的派别承诺永久放弃使用武力。
senses.why: The oath reaches beyond belief into behaviour; what is sworn off is a road, not only a thought.
senses.whyCN: 誓言不止及于信念，还及于行为；被誓绝的是一条路，而不只是一个念头。

senses.title: To disclaim or avoid deliberately
senses.definition: to avoid or reject something deliberately, an older general use
senses.definitionCN: 有意避开或拒绝某事物，属较旧的泛化用法
senses.example: She abjured all luxury during her years of study.
senses.exampleCN: 求学岁月里，她刻意摒弃一切奢华。
senses.why: A sworn avoidance carries the firmness of a vow even when no formal oath is spoken.
senses.whyCN: 郑重的回避即使没有正式起誓，也带着誓言般的坚定。

intro.en: Abjure is a Latin oath-word: ab-, away, plus iurare, to swear; renouncing is done by oath.
intro.cn: abjure 是拉丁语誓言词：ab-「离开」加 iurare「起誓」；弃绝以誓言完成。

items.en: The root yewes- related to solemn words and reverence is reconstructed.
items.cn: 与庄严言语、敬畏相关的原始印欧词根 yewes- 属重构形式。

items.en: Iurare meant to swear; abiurare meant to deny on oath.
items.cn: 拉丁语 iurare 意为起誓；abiurare 意为以誓否认。

items.en: Abiurer carried the legal-religious renunciation into French.
items.cn: 古法语 abiurer 把法律-宗教性的弃绝带入法语。

items.en: English borrowed abjure for sworn renunciations, especially of faith.
items.cn: 英语借入 abjure，专指宣誓弃绝，尤指信仰。

items.en: It survives as a formal, often historical, verb.
items.cn: 如今它作为正式且常带历史色彩的动词存留。

note.en: Abjure shares its iur- root with jury and perjury; it is often confused with adjure.
note.cn: abjure 的 iur- 词根与 jury、perjury 同族；它常与 adjure 混淆。

entries.definition: to solemnly urge someone, not renounce
entries.definitionCN: 郑重恳求、告诫；与 abjure 同根而意义相反方向

entries.definition: false swearing
entries.definitionCN: 伪证；同根 iurare 的负面形式

entries.definition: the formal act of abjuring
entries.definitionCN: 名词形式，义为誓绝

entries.definition: to give up formally, without the oath element
entries.definitionCN: 正式放弃；不强调誓言

entries.definition: to withdraw a former statement or belief
entries.definitionCN: 撤回前言；多指公开改口

entries.definition: to swear off or deny under oath
entries.definitionCN: 誓绝；与 abjure 最近的近义词

normalIntro.en: Five anchors tie abjure to the sworn farewell.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手把 abjure 与「宣誓告别」绑在一起。

normal.en: ab- away + jur- swear: swear something away.
normal.cn: ab-（离开）＋ jur-（起誓）：用誓言送走什么。

normal.en: jur- also lives in jury, justice family words.
normal.cn: jur- 也见于 jury 等司法词。

normal.en: Do not confuse with adjure, to urge solemnly.
normal.cn: 别与 adjure「郑重恳求」混淆。

normal.en: abjure violence: promise never again.
normal.cn: abjure violence：承诺永不再犯。

normal.en: recant is the twin for taking back words.
normal.cn: recant 是「收回言论」的孪生词。

abstract.en: See a signed parchment nailed to a door.
abstract.cn: 看见钉在门上的签署羊皮纸。

abstract.en: Hear a quill scratching a final farewell.
abstract.cn: 听见羽笔写下最后告别之声。

abstract.en: Feel an old letter burned in a bowl.
abstract.cn: 感到旧信在碗中烧尽的温度。

examples.en: The prisoners abjured their old loyalties before release.
examples.cn: 囚犯们在获释前宣誓放弃旧日的效忠。

examples.en: He abjured every form of dishonesty in his new position.
examples.cn: 他在新岗位上郑重戒绝一切不诚实的行为。

examples.en: Under oath, she abjured all claim to the estate.
examples.cn: 她在宣誓之下放弃了对那笔遗产的一切主张。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我不赌」——我对天发誓再也不赌了

root: 拉丁语 abiurare「以誓否认」＝ ab-「离开」＋ iurare「起誓」（词根 ius「法、誓」，出自重构的原始印欧词根 yewes-）。经古法语 abiurer 于十五世纪进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses widen one oath: a belief, a behaviour, and a deliberate avoidance.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项扩展同一份誓言：信念、行为、以及有意的回避。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand raised over a book, swearing a belief away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在书上，宣誓告别某个信念。

branches.en: THE BELIEF OATH: doctrine and allegiance are given up by vow.
branches.cn: 信念之誓：学说与效忠以誓言交出。

branches.en: THE BEHAVIOUR OATH: a road is closed by promise.
branches.cn: 行为之誓：一条路被承诺封死。

branches.en: THE QUIET VOW: everyday avoidance keeps the vow's firmness.
branches.cn: 无声之誓：日常的回避保持誓言般的坚定。

branches.en: UNDER OATH: both senses need the solemn, public form.
branches.cn: 在誓言之下：这两个义项都需要庄严公开的形式。

branches.en: ONE FAREWELL: every sense is a permanent goodbye sworn or felt.
branches.cn: 同一场告别：每个义项都是誓出的或心许的永久再见。

intro.en: An oath root with a leaving prefix; the Latin is still transparent.
intro.cn: 誓言词根加离开前缀；拉丁结构至今透明。

latinIntro.en: Latin iurare and abiurare are recorded; the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 iurare 与 abiurare 有记载；更深的印欧词根属重构形式。

items.example: It marks what is sworn off.
It is the twin to disentangle.
items.exampleCN: 它是需要辨析的孪生词。

items.example: It shows the root in law.
items.exampleCN: 它显示词根的法律用法。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ion 构成，义为「誓绝；弃国誓」
同根近形词，义为「郑重的恳求或告诫」

definition_zh: 放弃（权利、要求）；克制（欲望）；否认
definition_en: to give up or deny oneself a right, claim, or desire
core_image: 把到手的果子从掌心推出去
scene: 遗产分割那天，她第一个签了字。He chose to abnegate his share of the inheritance for the family's sake.
sceneCN: 这里 abnegate 是「放弃」（第 1 个义项：让出应得的权利）；句意为为了家人，他选择放弃自己那份遗产。

pos.zh: 克制、舍弃（自身欲望）；否认

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「克制；自我舍弃」
合成名词，义为「自我克制；忘我」

senses.title: To give up a right or claim
senses.definition: to formally give up a right, claim, or privilege
senses.definitionCN: 正式放弃权利、主张或特权
senses.example: The minister abnegated any claim to the disputed land.
senses.exampleCN: 部长放弃了对争议土地的一切主张。
senses.why: The Latin negare means to deny; abnegating a claim is saying no to what was yours.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 negare 意为否认；放弃主张就是对原本属于你的东西说「不」。

senses.title: To deny oneself desires
senses.definition: to refuse oneself pleasures or comforts, usually from principle
senses.definitionCN: 出于原则而拒绝给自己享受或安逸
senses.example: Monastic rules require monks to abnegate ordinary comforts.
senses.exampleCN: 修道会规要求修士舍弃寻常的舒适。
senses.why: Saying no turns inward: the same denial is applied to one's own wants.
senses.whyCN: 「说不」转向内部：同样的否定用在自身欲望上。

senses.title: To deny or disown a thing
senses.definition: to declare something untrue or refuse to acknowledge it
senses.definitionCN: 宣称某事不实或拒绝承认
senses.example: The board abnegated the rumours about merger plans.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会否认了有关合并计划的传闻。
senses.why: Denial is the verb root itself; pushing a statement away is the outermost use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 否认正是词根本义；把一个说法推开，是这个词最外层的用法。

intro.en: Abnegate joins Latin negare, to deny, with the away-prefix; saying no and pushing away at once.
intro.cn: abnegate 把拉丁语 negare「否认」与离开前缀结合：既说不，又推开。

items.en: A root for saying no, ne- plus a verbal ending, is reconstructed.
items.cn: 表示「说不」的词根 ne- 加动词词尾，属重构形式。

items.en: Negare meant to deny or refuse.
items.cn: 拉丁语 negare 意为否认、拒绝。

items.en: Abnegare meant to refuse something away from oneself, to renounce.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 abnegare 意为拒之于己外、弃绝。

items.en: Abnegate entered learned English, mostly religious in tone.
items.cn: 十七世纪 abnegate 进入学术英语，多带宗教色彩。

items.en: The noun abnegation is now more common than the verb.
items.cn: 如今名词 abnegation 比动词更常用。

note.en: Abnegate belongs to the neg- deny family and is often met as the noun abnegation.
note.cn: abnegate 属于 neg-「否认」词族，更常见的形态是名词 abnegation。

entries.definition: self-denial or renunciation
entries.definitionCN: 名词形式，义为克制、自我舍弃

entries.definition: to nullify or deny, without the away-prefix
entries.definitionCN: 否定、使无效；同根 negare 但无离开前缀

entries.definition: third-person form of the verb
entries.definitionCN: 动词三单形式

entries.definition: to give up formally
entries.definitionCN: 正式放弃；不带否认色彩

entries.definition: to give up a pleasure or advantage
entries.definitionCN: 放弃享受；语域更日常

entries.definition: the practice of refusing oneself pleasures
entries.definitionCN: 自我克制的做法；对应第 2 义项

normalIntro.en: Five anchors tie abnegate to the pushed-away fruit.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手把 abnegate 与被推开的果实绑在一起。

normal.en: ab- away + neg- deny: deny and push away.
normal.cn: ab-（离开）＋ neg-（否认）：既说不又推开。

normal.en: neg- family: negative, negate, neglect.
normal.cn: neg- 词族：negative、negate、neglect。

normal.en: abnegation of self: monastic word.
normal.cn: abnegation of self：修道用语。

normal.en: Abnegate rights: say no to your own claim.
normal.cn: abnegate rights：对自己的主张说不。

normal.en: The noun is commoner than the verb today.
normal.cn: 如今名词比动词常用。

abstract.en: Feel a ripe apple pushed across the table.
abstract.cn: 感到一只熟苹果被推过桌面。

abstract.en: Hear a firm no said to oneself.
abstract.cn: 听见对自己说出的坚定「不」。

abstract.en: See a door closed on a comfort.
abstract.cn: 看见一扇门对着安逸关上。

examples.en: He abnegated his claim to the family estate.
examples.cn: 他放弃了对家族产业的主张。

examples.en: The discipline required them to abnegate every luxury.
examples.cn: 戒律要求他们舍弃一切奢华。

examples.en: A life of abnegation shaped her plain habits.
examples.cn: 克己的生活塑造了她朴素的习惯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我不内给」——我对自己说：不内给，好东西先推出去

root: 拉丁语 abnegare「拒之于外」＝ ab-「离开」＋ negare「否认」（词根出自重构的原始印欧 ne-「不」）。经晚期拉丁语于十七世纪进入英语；名词 abnegation 常表「克己」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses aim one no in three directions: at a claim, at a desire, at a statement.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项把同一个「不」指向三个方向：主张、欲望、说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ripe fruit pushed off the palm.
core.cn: 核心意象：熟果被从掌心推开。

branches.en: THE CLAIM: outward rights are the first to be refused.
branches.cn: 主张：外在的权利首先被拒绝。

branches.en: THE DESIRE: the no turns inward on one's own wants.
branches.cn: 欲望：这个「不」转向自身欲望。

branches.en: THE STATEMENT: denial pushed furthest, at truth claims.
branches.cn: 说法：否认推得最远，指向真伪判断。

branches.en: GIVING UP: both senses are refusals of what one could have.
branches.cn: 舍弃：这两个义项都是对可得之物的拒绝。

branches.en: ONE NO: every sense is negare carrying the away-prefix.
branches.cn: 同一个「不」：每个义项都是带着离开前缀的 negare。

intro.en: A denial root with a leaving prefix; the family is easy to map.
intro.cn: 否认词根加离开前缀；词族脉络清晰。

latinIntro.en: Latin negare is classical; the Indo-European ne- particle is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 negare 见于古典文献；印欧小品词 ne- 属重构。

items.example: It is the reconstructed ancestor of neg-.
items.exampleCN: 它是 neg- 的重构祖先。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ion 构成，义为「克制；自我舍弃」
合成名词，义为「自我克制；忘我」

definition_zh: 反常的；异常的；不正常的；畸形的
definition_en: different from what is usual, expected, or healthy, especially in a way that causes concern
core_image: 一排整齐的方砖里，被塞进了一块尺寸不对的砖
scene: 体检报告上有一项数值高得离谱，医生又让人重测了一次。The scan showed an abnormal growth on the left side of the lung.
sceneCN: 这里 abnormal 指医学检查中的异常（第 1 个义项：身体上的异常）；句意为扫描显示左肺有一处异常增生。

pos.zh: 反常的；异常的；不正常的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「异常地；反常地」
由形容词加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「异常；畸形」

senses.title: Not normal in the body
senses.definition: of a body part, cell, or growth, differing from what is healthy or usual
senses.definitionCN: 指身体部位、细胞或增生与健康、常见状态不同
senses.example: The test found abnormal cells in the sample.
senses.exampleCN: 检测在样本中发现了异常细胞。
senses.why: The Latin root names a carpenter's square, the tool that tests whether a line is true; cells that fail the test are abnormal.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根指木匠的曲尺，是用来检验线条是否端正的工具；通不过检验的细胞就是异常。

senses.title: Deviating from usual behaviour
senses.definition: of behaviour or mental state, far from what is typical for a person or a group
senses.definitionCN: 指行为或心理状态远离一个人或群体的常见样子
senses.example: His abnormal silence worried his friends.
senses.exampleCN: 他反常的沉默让朋友们担心。
senses.why: Behaviour is measured against what a group treats as the norm, and the word marks the distance from that line.
senses.whyCN: 行为以群体当作常规的尺度来衡量，这个词标记的就是偏离那条线的距离。

senses.title: Outside the expected range
senses.definition: of a measurement or reading, lying outside the range that is considered safe or typical
senses.definitionCN: 指测量值或读数落在被认为安全、正常范围之外
senses.example: The sensor recorded an abnormal rise in temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器记录到温度的异常上升。
senses.why: A scale has a normal band, and any reading off that band is described with the same word used for bodies.
senses.whyCN: 刻度上有一段正常区间，落在区间之外的读数，就用描述身体的那个词来说。

senses.title: Rare in nature
senses.definition: of a natural event, occurring far less often than usual or outside its normal pattern
senses.definitionCN: 指自然事件出现得远少于平常，或脱离其常见规律
senses.example: An abnormal tide wiped out the lower path.
senses.exampleCN: 一场反常的潮水冲毁了低处的小路。
senses.why: Nature has a rhythm, and an event that breaks the rhythm is called abnormal even when nothing is wrong with it.
senses.whyCN: 自然有节奏，打破节奏的事件即便本身无害，也被称为反常。

intro.en: Abnormal is a Latin phrase made into an English adjective: away from the rule, with the rule itself imagined as a carpenter's square.
intro.cn: abnormal 是把一个拉丁短语做成了英语形容词：离开规则，而规则本身被想象成木匠的曲尺。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for anything outside the normal range, from cells to weather, and the adverb abnormally is common in reports.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指任何超出正常范围的东西，从细胞到天气；副词 abnormally 在报告里很常见。

items.en: The adjective is recorded in English in the early nineteenth century, formed on the French model rather than inherited from Latin.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十九世纪初见于英语，是照法语样式构成，而不是直接从拉丁语继承。

items.en: French anormal, itself from Latin, supplied the pattern for the English word.
items.cn: 法语 anormal 本身来自拉丁语，为英语词提供了构词样式。

items.en: Latin abnormis meant irregular or departing from rule, built from ab- meaning away from and norma meaning rule.
items.cn: 拉丁语 abnormis 意为「不合规则、离开规则」，由表示「离开」的 ab- 与表示「规则」的 norma 构成。

items.en: Norma was a carpenter's square, the tool that keeps a line true, and it also gave English norm and normal.
items.cn: norma 是木匠的曲尺，是用来让线条端正的工具，它还给英语带来了 norm 与 normal。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin rule; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for things outside the usual pattern.
note.cn: 形近组收建在拉丁语「规则」上的词；近义组收表示脱离常见样式的形容词。

entries.definition: Something that deviates from the standard, but built on a Greek root instead.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「异常事物」，但建在希腊词根上。

entries.definition: Deviating from the normal order, the adjective matching anomaly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「反常的」，与 anomaly 对应。

entries.definition: In a way that departs from the usual or healthy pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「异常地、反常地」。

entries.definition: The standard that a group treats as normal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「规范、常态」，指群体视为正常的标准。

entries.definition: Not common, but often neutral rather than worrying.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不寻常的」，语气常是中性的，不带担忧。

entries.definition: Not following the normal pattern in shape, time, or behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不规则的」，形状、时间或行为不合常规。

entries.definition: Departing from what is normal or acceptable, often of behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「越轨的、异常的」，多用于行为。

entries.definition: Not representative of its type, a milder and more clinical word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「非典型的」，语气更轻、更偏临床。

entries.definition: Strange and unnatural in a way that shocks or amuses.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「怪异的」，带令人惊讶或觉得好笑的意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin parts of the word and the places where it appears in ordinary life.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词的拉丁构件，以及它在日常生活中出现的场合。

normal.en: ab- means away from and normal means according to rule, so abnormal is simply away from the rule.
normal.cn: ab- 表示「离开」，normal 表示「合乎规则」，所以 abnormal 就是离开规则。

normal.en: Norma was a carpenter's square, the tool that tests a right angle; abnormal is the line that will not square.
normal.cn: norma 是木匠的曲尺，用来检验直角；abnormal 就是那条怎么量都不正的线。

normal.en: Anomaly is the noun and anomalous the adjective of the same idea, both built on Greek rather than Latin.
normal.cn: anomaly 是名词，anomalous 是形容词，表达同一意念，但两者建在希腊语而不是拉丁语上。

normal.en: Hospitals use abnormal for test results, and the word there is neutral, not an insult.
normal.cn: 医院用 abnormal 说检查结果，那里的语气是中性的，并不是骂人。

normal.en: Abnormal psychology is the fixed course name for the study of behaviour far from usual patterns.
normal.cn: abnormal psychology 是固定课程名，研究远离常见模式的行为。

abstract.en: Picture a row of identical tiles with one tile of the wrong size pushed into the line.
abstract.cn: 想象一排一模一样的砖，其中被塞进了一块尺寸不对的砖。

abstract.en: The gap it makes is what the eye notices first, before it can say what is wrong.
abstract.cn: 眼睛最先注意到的是它挤出的缝隙，然后才说得出哪里不对。

abstract.en: The same misfit tile appears in a blood test, a storm, and a design that breaks the pattern.
abstract.cn: 同一块不合尺寸的砖，会出现在血液检查、风暴，以及打破样式的设计里。

examples.en: The doctor ordered more tests after the abnormal result.
examples.cn: 结果异常之后，医生安排了更多检查。

examples.en: Such abnormal rainfall has not been seen in this region for decades.
examples.cn: 这种反常的降雨在这个地区几十年未见。

examples.en: The report described the sudden change in policy as abnormal.
examples.cn: 报告称政策的突然变化不合常规。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布诺」——阿布在一排整齐的砖里站错了位置

root: 拉丁语 abnormis「不合规则」＝ ab-「离开」＋ norma「曲尺、规范」；norma 还是英语 norm 与 normal 的来源。英语形容词见于十九世纪初，受法语 anormal 影响而成。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses apply one ruler, the normal range, to a body, a behaviour, a reading and a season.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项用同一把尺子「正常范围」，去量身体、行为、读数和季节。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one tile of the wrong size is pushed into a row of identical tiles.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块尺寸不对的砖被塞进一排整齐相同的砖里。

branches.en: THE BODY: a cell that fails the carpenter's square is marked abnormal.
branches.cn: 身体线：通不过曲尺检验的细胞就被标为异常。

branches.en: THE BEHAVIOUR: the group supplies the line that the person departs from.
branches.cn: 行为线：群体提供那条被人偏离的线。

branches.en: THE READING: a scale has a normal band, and values outside it take the same word.
branches.cn: 读数线：刻度上有一段正常区间，区间外的数值也用这个词。

branches.en: THE SEASON: nature keeps a rhythm, and weather that ignores it is called abnormal.
branches.cn: 季节线：自然自有节奏，无视节奏的天气就被称作反常。

branches.en: THE SHARED RULER: every sense is a distance measured from an expected line.
branches.cn: 共同线：每个义项都是偏离一条预期线之后量出的距离。

intro.en: The word is Latin from end to end, with only the adjective ending added in English.
intro.cn: 这个词从头到尾都是拉丁语，英语只加了形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin norma, abnormis and normalis are recorded, so the parts are historical rather than reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 norma、abnormis 与 normalis 都有文献记录，因此这些构件属于有史可查的形式。

items.example: It marks departure from the rule.
It is the rule against which things are measured.
items.exampleCN: 它是用来衡量事物的那把尺。

items.example: It is the short English form of the Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: 它是那个拉丁名词的英语短形式。

items.example: It is the positive word that abnormal negates.
items.exampleCN: 它是 abnormal 所否定的正面词。

items.example: It is the Latin source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语词的拉丁语来源。

items.example: It forms abnormal from the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 它把拉丁词干构成 abnormal。

items.example: It expresses the same idea from a Greek root.
items.exampleCN: 它从希腊词根表达同一意念。

latinEntries.meaning: made according to a square, regular

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「异常地；反常地」
由形容词加 -ity 构成，义为「异常；畸形」

definition_zh: 令人憎恶的；可恶的；糟透的
definition_en: causing disgust or hatred; extremely bad or unpleasant
core_image: 一盆残羹被打翻，臭味让满桌人捂鼻
scene: 包厢里烟味浓得呛人，邻座还在吞云吐雾。The passengers endured the abominable smell in the carriage.
sceneCN: 这里 abominable 是「糟透的、令人厌恶的」（第 2 个义项：状况极差令人不适）；句意为乘客们忍受着车厢里恶劣难闻的气味。

pos.zh: 令人憎恶的；可恶的（道德上）
糟透的；恶劣的（程度、状况）

collocations.zh: 雪人（喜马拉雅传说中的怪物）

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「憎恶；痛恨」
同根名词，义为「憎恶之物；可憎的行为」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「可恶地；恶劣地」

senses.title: Morally hateful
senses.definition: deserving strong dislike because it is evil or violates what people hold sacred
senses.definitionCN: 因其邪恶或触犯人们敬重之物而应受强烈憎恶
senses.example: The old law branded such betrayal an abominable crime.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时法律把这种背叛定为可憎的罪行。
senses.why: Folk etymology heard ab homine, away from man; what falls below humanity is hated as less than human.
senses.whyCN: 民间词源把它听成 ab homine「远离人」；堕落到人之下者，被当作非人之物憎恨。

senses.title: Extremely unpleasant in degree
senses.definition: of conditions, behaviour, or quality, extremely bad or unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 指状况、行为或品质极差、令人难受
senses.example: The troops marched through abominable mud and rain.
senses.exampleCN: 部队在糟透的泥泞和冷雨中行军。
senses.why: Hate soaks into everyday life; weather, manners, and smells borrow the strong word for their worst forms.
senses.whyCN: 憎恶渗入日常生活；天气、举止与气味借用这个强烈的词形容它们最坏的形态。

intro.en: Abominable comes from Latin abominari, to deprecate as an ill omen; the ab homine story is a folk myth.
intro.cn: abominable 来自拉丁语 abominari「视为凶兆而远离」；「远离人」的说法是民间讹传。

items.en: A root for omens, os- men-, is reconstructed behind the Latin word.
items.cn: 拉丁词背后重构出一个表示「兆象」的词根 os-men-。

items.en: Abominari meant to avert, to deprecate as an omen of ill.
items.cn: 拉丁语 abominari 意为避开、视之为凶兆而祈禳。

items.en: Ablominable or abominable passed into French learned use.
items.cn: abominable 以学术用法进入古法语。

items.en: English took it for things hateful to God and man.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语借入该词，指神人所憎之事。

items.en: Folk spelling abominable < ab-hominable persisted, feeding the myth.
items.cn: 民间拼法 abominable→ab-hominable 长期存在，助长了讹传。

note.en: Abominable is often mis-split as ab-hominable; its true root speaks of omens.
note.cn: abominable 常被误拆为 ab-hominable；其真正的词根说的是「兆象」。

entries.definition: something loathed
entries.definitionCN: 名词形式，义为憎恶之物

entries.definition: to loathe
entries.definitionCN: 动词形式，义为憎恶

entries.definition: of names; shares letters but comes from nomen
entries.definitionCN: 名义上的；来自 nomen「名字」，词源完全不同

entries.definition: deserving intense dislike
entries.definitionCN: 可憎的；语域相近

entries.definition: arousing disgust or aversion
entries.definitionCN: 令人反感的；偏重生理与心理排斥

entries.definition: shockingly bad or brutal
entries.definitionCN: 恶劣残暴的；常指程度

normalIntro.en: Five anchors tie abominable to the turned-away face.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手把 abominable 与扭开的脸绑在一起。

normal.en: a- + bomin(o)- omen: turn from a bad omen.
normal.cn: a- ＋ bomin（兆象）：远离凶兆。

normal.en: Watch out: not ab + human, that is folk myth.
normal.cn: 注意：不是 ab＋human，那是民间讹传。

normal.en: Abominable Snowman is the famous name.
normal.cn: 「雪人」是最著名的用例。

normal.en: abominable weather: British favourite for bad skies.
normal.cn: abominable weather：英国人说天气糟透的口头禅。

normal.en: abomination is the noun to pair.
normal.cn: 配对的名词是 abomination。

abstract.en: Smell spoiled soup and step back.
abstract.cn: 闻到馊汤味，退后半步。

abstract.en: See umbrellas breaking in grey gales.
abstract.cn: 看见雨伞在灰暗的狂风里折断。

abstract.en: Feel eyes narrow at a cruel act.
abstract.cn: 感到目睹恶行时眯起的双眼。

examples.en: Slave trafficking was condemned as an abominable trade.
examples.cn: 贩卖奴隶被斥为可憎的行当。

examples.en: We cancelled the picnic because of abominable weather.
examples.cn: 天气恶劣，我们取消了野餐。

examples.en: His abominable manners cost him every dinner invitation.
examples.cn: 他那糟糕透顶的举止让他失去了所有晚宴邀约。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我报你难啵」——我忍不住报怨：你也太难闻了吧

root: 拉丁语 abominari「视为凶兆而祈禳远离」＝ ab-「离开」＋ omen「兆象」＋ 动词后缀 -ari。「ab homine（远离人）」一说为民间词源讹传。经古法语于十四世纪进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses spread one aversion: from sacred hatred down to everyday awfulness.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项扩展同一种厌恶：从神圣的憎恶降到日常的糟糕。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face turning away and a hand waving off the stench.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张扭开的脸，一只挥散恶臭的手。

branches.en: THE SACRED LINE: what breaks the revered is hated outright.
branches.cn: 神圣之线：触犯敬重之物者遭彻底憎恨。

branches.en: THE WEATHER REPORT: ordinary badness borrows the strong word.
branches.cn: 天气预报：日常的糟糕借用了这个强词。

branches.en: ONE AVERSION: both senses push the face away.
branches.cn: 同一种厌恶：两个义项都把脸扭开。

branches.en: INTENSIFIER ROLE: the word doubles as a strengthener for bad nouns.
branches.cn: 强化语角色：该词兼作强化修饰语。

branches.en: FROM OMENS TO WEATHER: the holy origin still glows beneath common use.
branches.cn: 从兆象到天气：神圣来源在日常用法下仍隐约发光。

intro.en: An omen root with a leaving prefix; the human-split is a false friend.
intro.cn: 兆象词根加离开前缀；「人类」的拆分是假朋友。

latinIntro.en: Latin abominari and omen are classical; the ab-homine derivation is disproved folk lore.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abominari 与 omen 见于古典文献；ab-homine 的推导已被证明是民间讹传。

items.example: It is wrongly used to split the word.
items.exampleCN: 它被错误地用来拆分该词。
